P3para.Text: of the registered holder of any such debentures, or any holder of shares in the company, without charge, and
of any other person on payment of such fee as may be prescribed.

P2para.Text: Any person may require a copy of the register, or any part of it, on payment of such fee as may be prescribed.
A person seeking to exercise either of the rights conferred by this section must make a request to the company to that effect.
The request must contain the following information—

P3para.Text: in the case of an individual, his name and address;
in the case of an organisation, the name and address of an individual responsible for making the request on behalf of the organisation;
the purpose for which the information is to be used; and
whether the information will be disclosed to any other person, and if so—

P4para.Text: where that person is an individual, his name and address,
where that person is an organisation, the name and address of an individual responsible for receiving the information on its behalf, and
the purpose for which the information is to be used by that person.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this section a register is “duly closed” if it is closed in accordance with provision contained—

P3para.Text: in the articles or in the debentures,
in the case of debenture stock in the stock certificates, or
in the trust deed or other document securing the debentures or debenture stock.

P2para.Text: The total period for which a register is closed in any year must not exceed 30 days.
References in this section to a register of debenture holders include a duplicate—

P3para.Text: of a register of debenture holders that is kept outside the United Kingdom, or
of any part of such a register.

P1group.Title: Register of debenture holders: response to request for inspection or copy

P2para.Text: Where a company receives a request under section 744 (register of debenture holders: right to inspect and require copy), it must within five working days either—

P3para.Text: comply with the request, or
apply to the court.

P2para.Text: If it applies to the court it must notify the person making the request.
If on an application under this section the court is satisfied that the inspection or copy is not sought for a proper purpose—

P3para.Text: it shall direct the company not to comply with the request, and
it may further order that the company's costs (in Scotland, expenses) on the application be paid in whole or in part by the person who made the request, even if he is not a party to the application.

P2para.Text: If the court makes such a direction and it appears to the court that the company is or may be subject to other requests made for a similar purpose (whether made by the same person or different persons), it may direct that the company is not to comply with any such request.
The order must contain such provision as appears to the court appropriate to identify the requests to which it applies.

If on an application under this section the court does not direct the company not to comply with the request, the company must comply with the request immediately upon the court giving its decision or, as the case may be, the proceedings being discontinued.

P1group.Title: Register of debenture holders: refusal of inspection or default in providing copy

P2para.Text: If an inspection required under section 744 (register of debenture holders: right to inspect and require copy) is refused or default is made in providing a copy required under that section, otherwise than in accordance with an order of the court, an offence is committed by—

P3para.Text: the company, and
every officer of the company who is in default.

P2para.Text: A person guilty of an offence under this section is liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding level 3 on the standard scale and, for continued contravention, a daily default fine not exceeding one-tenth of level 3 on the standard scale.
In the case of any such refusal or default the court may by order compel an immediate inspection or, as the case may be, direct that the copy required be sent to the person requesting it.

P1group.Title: Register of debenture holders: offences in connection with request for or disclosure of information

P2para.Text: It is an offence for a person knowingly or recklessly to make in a request under section 744 (register of debenture holders: right to inspect and require copy) a statement that is misleading, false or deceptive in a material particular.
It is an offence for a person in possession of information obtained by exercise of either of the rights conferred by that section—

P3para.Text: to do anything that results in the information being disclosed to another person, or
to fail to do anything with the result that the information is disclosed to another person,

P2para.Text: knowing, or having reason to suspect, that person may use the information for a purpose that is not a proper purpose.
A person guilty of an offence under this section is liable—

P3para.Text: on conviction on indictment, to imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years or a fine (or both);
on summary conviction—

P4para.Text: in England and Wales, to imprisonment for a term not exceeding twelve months or to a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum (or both);
in Scotland or Northern Ireland, to imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months, or to a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum (or both).

P1group.Title: Time limit for claims arising from entry in register

P2para.Text: Liability incurred by a company—

P3para.Text: from the making or deletion of an entry in the register of debenture holders, or
from a failure to make or delete any such entry,

P2para.Text: is not enforceable more than ten years after the date on which the entry was made or deleted or, as the case may be, the failure first occurred.
This is without prejudice to any lesser period of limitation (and, in Scotland, to any rule that the obligation giving rise to the liability prescribes before the expiry of that period).

P1group.Title: Right of debenture holder to copy of deed

P2para.Text: Any holder of debentures of a company is entitled, on request and on payment of such fee as may be prescribed, to be provided with a copy of any trust deed for securing the debentures.
If default is made in complying with this section, an offence is committed by every officer of the company who is in default.

A person guilty of an offence under this section is liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding level 3 on the standard scale and, for continued contravention, a daily default fine not exceeding one-tenth of level 3 on the standard scale.
In the case of any such default the court may direct that the copy required be sent to the person requiring it.

P1group.Title: Liability of trustees of debentures

P2para.Text: Any provision contained in—

P3para.Text: a trust deed for securing an issue of debentures, or
any contract with the holders of debentures secured by a trust deed,

P2para.Text: is void in so far as it would have the effect of exempting a trustee of the deed from, or indemnifying him against, liability for breach of trust where he fails to show the degree of care and diligence required of him as trustee, having regard to the provisions of the trust deed conferring on him any powers, authorities or discretions.
Subsection (1) does not invalidate—

P3para.Text: a release otherwise validly given in respect of anything done or omitted to be done by a trustee before the giving of the release;
any provision enabling such a release to be given—

P4para.Text: on being agreed to by a majority of not less than 75% in value of the debenture holders present and voting in person or, where proxies are permitted, by proxy at a meeting summoned for the purpose, and
either with respect to specific acts or omissions or on the trustee dying or ceasing to act.

P2para.Text: This section is subject to section 751 (saving for certain older provisions).

P1group.Title: Liability of trustees of debentures: saving for certain older provisions

P2para.Text: Section 750 (liability of trustees of debentures) does not operate—

P3para.Text: to invalidate any provision in force on the relevant date so long as any person—

P4para.Text: then entitled to the benefit of the provision, or
afterwards given the benefit of the provision under subsection (3) below,

P3para.Text: remains a trustee of the deed in question, or
to deprive any person of any exemption or right to be indemnified in respect of anything done or omitted to be done by him while any such provision was in force.

P2para.Text: The relevant date for this purpose is—

P3para.Text: 1st July 1948 in a case where section 192 of the Companies Act 1985 (c. 6) applied immediately before the commencement of this section;
1st July 1961 in a case where Article 201 of the Companies (Northern Ireland) Order 1986 (S.I. 1986/1032 (N.I. 6)) then applied.

P2para.Text: While any trustee of a trust deed remains entitled to the benefit of a provision saved by subsection (1) above the benefit of that provision may be given either—

P3para.Text: to all trustees of the deed, present and future, or
to any named trustees or proposed trustees of it,

P2para.Text: by a resolution passed by a majority of not less than 75% in value of the debenture holders present in person or, where proxies are permitted, by proxy at a meeting summoned for the purpose.
A meeting for that purpose must be summoned in accordance with the provisions of the deed or, if the deed makes no provision for summoning meetings, in a manner approved by the court.

P1group.Title: Power to re-issue redeemed debentures

P2para.Text: Where a company has redeemed debentures previously issued, then unless—

P3para.Text: provision to the contrary (express or implied) is contained in the company's articles or in any contract made by the company, or
the company has, by passing a resolution to that effect or by some other act, manifested its intention that the debentures shall be cancelled,

P2para.Text: the company may re-issue the debentures, either by re-issuing the same debentures or by issuing new debentures in their place.
This subsection is deemed always to have had effect.
On a re-issue of redeemed debentures the person entitled to the debentures has (and is deemed always to have had) the same priorities as if the debentures had never been redeemed.
The re-issue of a debenture or the issue of another debenture in its place under this section is treated as the issue of a new debenture for the purposes of stamp duty.
It is not so treated for the purposes of any provision limiting the amount or number of debentures to be issued.

A person lending money on the security of a debenture re-issued under this section which appears to be duly stamped may give the debenture in evidence in any proceedings for enforcing his security without payment of the stamp duty or any penalty in respect of it, unless he had notice (or, but for his negligence, might have discovered) that the debenture was not duly stamped.
In that case the company is liable to pay the proper stamp duty and penalty.

P1group.Title: Deposit of debentures to secure advances

P1para.Text: Where a company has deposited any of its debentures to secure advances from time to time on current account or otherwise, the debentures are not treated as redeemed by reason only of the company's account having ceased to be in debit while the debentures remained so deposited.

P1group.Title: Priorities where debentures secured by floating charge

P2para.Text: This section applies where debentures of a company registered in England and Wales or Northern Ireland are secured by a charge that, as created, was a floating charge.

If possession is taken, by or on behalf of the holders of the debentures, of any property comprised in or subject to the charge, and the company is not at that time in the course of being wound up, the company's preferential debts shall be paid out of assets coming to the hands of the persons taking possession in priority to any claims for principal or interest in respect of the debentures.
“Preferential debts” means the categories of debts listed in Schedule 6 to the Insolvency Act 1986 (c. 45) or Schedule 4 to the Insolvency (Northern Ireland) Order 1989 (S.I. 1989/2405 (N.I. 19)).
For the purposes of those Schedules “the relevant date” is the date of possession being taken as mentioned in subsection (2).
Payments under this section shall be recouped, as far as may be, out of the assets of the company available for payment of general creditors.

Chapter.Title: Prohibition of public offers by private companies

P1group.Title: Prohibition of public offers by private company

P2para.Text: A private company limited by shares or limited by guarantee and having a share capital must not—

P3para.Text: offer to the public any securities of the company, or
allot or agree to allot any securities of the company with a view to their being offered to the public.

P2para.Text: Unless the contrary is proved, an allotment or agreement to allot securities is presumed to be made with a view to their being offered to the public if an offer of the securities (or any of them) to the public is made—

P3para.Text: within six months after the allotment or agreement to allot, or
before the receipt by the company of the whole of the consideration to be received by it in respect of the securities.

P2para.Text: A company does not contravene this section if—

P3para.Text: it acts in good faith in pursuance of arrangements under which it is to re-register as a public company before the securities are allotted, or
as part of the terms of the offer it undertakes to re-register as a public company within a specified period, and that undertaking is complied with.

P2para.Text: The specified period for the purposes of subsection (3)(b) must be a period ending not later than six months after the day on which the offer is made (or, in the case of an offer made on different days, first made).
In this Chapter “securities” means shares or debentures.

P1group.Title: Meaning of “offer to the public”

P2para.Text: This section explains what is meant in this Chapter by an offer of securities to the public.
An offer to the public includes an offer to any section of the public, however selected.
An offer is not regarded as an offer to the public if it can properly be regarded, in all the circumstances, as—

P3para.Text: not being calculated to result, directly or indirectly, in securities of the company becoming available to persons other than those receiving the offer, or
otherwise being a private concern of the person receiving it and the person making it.

P2para.Text: An offer is to be regarded (unless the contrary is proved) as being a private concern of the person receiving it and the person making it if—

P3para.Text: it is made to a person already connected with the company and, where it is made on terms allowing that person to renounce his rights, the rights may only be renounced in favour of another person already connected with the company; or

it is an offer to subscribe for securities to be held under an employees' share scheme and, where it is made on terms allowing that person to renounce his rights, the rights may only be renounced in favour of—

P4para.Text: another person entitled to hold securities under the scheme, or
a person already connected with the company.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this section “person already connected with the company” means—

P3para.Text: an existing member or employee of the company,
a member of the family of a person who is or was a member or employee of the company,
the widow or widower, or surviving civil partner, of a person who was a member or employee of the company,
an existing debenture holder of the company, or
a trustee (acting in his capacity as such) of a trust of which the principal beneficiary is a person within any of paragraphs (a) to (d).

P2para.Text: For the purposes of subsection (5)(b) the members of a person's family are the person's spouse or civil partner and children (including step-children) and their descendants.

P1group.Title: Enforcement of prohibition: order restraining proposed contravention

P2para.Text: If it appears to the court—

P3para.Text: on an application under this section, or
in proceedings under Part 30 (protection of members against unfair prejudice),

P2para.Text: that a company is proposing to act in contravention of section 755 (prohibition of public offers by private companies), the court shall make an order under this section.
An order under this section is an order restraining the company from contravening that section.
An application for an order under this section may be made by—

P3para.Text: a member or creditor of the company, or
the Secretary of State.

P1group.Title: Enforcement of prohibition: orders available to the court after contravention

P2para.Text: This section applies if it appears to the court—

P3para.Text: on an application under this section, or
in proceedings under Part 30 (protection of members against unfair prejudice),

P2para.Text: that a company has acted in contravention of section 755 (prohibition of public offers by private companies).
The court must make an order requiring the company to re-register as a public company unless it appears to the court—

P3para.Text: that the company does not meet the requirements for re-registration as a public company, and
that it is impractical or undesirable to require it to take steps to do so.

P2para.Text: If it does not make an order for re-registration, the court may make either or both of the following—

P3para.Text: a remedial order (see section 759), or
an order for the compulsory winding up of the company.

P2para.Text: An application under this section may be made by—

P3para.Text: a member of the company who—

P4para.Text: was a member at the time the offer was made (or, if the offer was made over a period, at any time during that period), or
became a member as a result of the offer,

P3para.Text: a creditor of the company who was a creditor at the time the offer was made (or, if the offer was made over a period, at any time during that period), or
the Secretary of State.

P1group.Title: Enforcement of prohibition: remedial order

P2para.Text: A “remedial order” is an order for the purpose of putting a person affected by anything done in contravention of section 755 (prohibition of public offers by private company) in the position he would have been in if it had not been done.
The following provisions are without prejudice to the generality of the power to make such an order.
Where a private company has—

P3para.Text: allotted securities pursuant to an offer to the public, or
allotted or agreed to allot securities with a view to their being offered to the public,

P2para.Text: a remedial order may require any person knowingly concerned in the contravention of section 755 to offer to purchase any of those securities at such price and on such other terms as the court thinks fit.
A remedial order may be made—

P3para.Text: against any person knowingly concerned in the contravention, whether or not an officer of the company;
notwithstanding anything in the company's constitution (which includes, for this purpose, the terms on which any securities of the company are allotted or held);
whether or not the holder of the securities subject to the order is the person to whom the company allotted or agreed to allot them.

P2para.Text: Where a remedial order is made against the company itself, the court may provide for the reduction of the company's capital accordingly.

P1group.Title: Validity of allotment etc not affected

P1para.Text: Nothing in this Chapter affects the validity of any allotment or sale of securities or of any agreement to allot or sell securities.

Chapter.Title: Minimum share capital requirement for public companies

P1group.Title: Public company: requirement as to minimum share capital

P2para.Text: A company that is a public company (otherwise than by virtue of re-registration as a public company) must not do business or exercise any borrowing powers unless the registrar has issued it with a certificate under this section (a “trading certificate”).

The registrar shall issue a trading certificate if, on an application made in accordance with section 762, he is satisfied that the nominal value of the company's allotted share capital is not less than the authorised minimum.
For this purpose a share allotted in pursuance of an employees' share scheme shall not be taken into account unless paid up as to—

P3para.Text: at least one-quarter of the nominal value of the share, and
the whole of any premium on the share.

P2para.Text: A trading certificate has effect from the date on which it is issued and is conclusive evidence that the company is entitled to do business and exercise any borrowing powers.

P1group.Title: Procedure for obtaining certificate

P2para.Text: An application for a certificate under section 761 must—

P3para.Text: state that the nominal value of the company's allotted share capital is not less than the authorised minimum,
specify the amount, or estimated amount, of the company's preliminary expenses,
specify any amount or benefit paid or given, or intended to be paid or given, to any promoter of the company, and the consideration for the payment or benefit, ...
be accompanied by a statement of compliance and

Text.Addition: be accompanied by a statement of the aggregate amount paid up on the shares of the company on account of their nominal value.

P2para.Text: The statement of compliance is a statement that the company meets the requirements for the issue of a certificate under section 761.
The registrar may accept the statement of compliance as sufficient evidence of the matters stated in it.

P1group.Title: The authorised minimum

P2para.Text: “The authorised minimum”, in relation to the nominal value of a public company's allotted share capital is—

P3para.Text: the prescribed euro equivalent.

P2para.Text: The Secretary of State may by order prescribe the amount in euros that is for the time being to be treated as equivalent to the sterling amount of the authorised minimum.
This power may be exercised from time to time as appears to the Secretary of State to be appropriate.
The amount prescribed shall be determined by applying an appropriate spot rate of exchange to the sterling amount and rounding to the nearest 100 euros.
An order under this section is subject to negative resolution procedure.
This section has effect subject to any exercise of the power conferred by section 764 (power to alter authorised minimum).

P1group.Title: Power to alter authorised minimum

P2para.Text: The Secretary of State may by order—

P3para.Text: alter the sterling amount of the authorised minimum, and
make a corresponding alteration of the prescribed euro equivalent.

P2para.Text: The amount of the prescribed euro equivalent shall be determined by applying an appropriate spot rate of exchange to the sterling amount and rounding to the nearest 100 euros.
An order under this section that increases the authorised minimum may—

P3para.Text: require a public company having an allotted share capital of which the nominal value is less than the amount specified in the order to—

P4para.Text: increase that value to not less than that amount, or
re-register as a private company;

P3para.Text: make provision in connection with any such requirement for any of the matters for which provision is made by this Act relating to—

P4para.Text: a company's registration, re-registration or change of name,
payment for shares comprised in a company's share capital, and
offers to the public of shares in or debentures of a company,

P3para.Text: including provision as to the consequences (in criminal law or otherwise) of a failure to comply with any requirement of the order;
provide for any provision of the order to come into force on different days for different purposes.

P2para.Text: An order under this section is subject to affirmative resolution procedure.

P1group.Title: Authorised minimum: application of initial requirement

P2para.Text: The initial requirement for a public company to have allotted share capital of a nominal value not less than the authorised minimum, that is—

P3para.Text: the requirement in section 761(2) for the issue of a trading certificate, or
the requirement in section 91(1)(a) for re-registration as a public company,

P2para.Text: must be met either by reference to allotted share capital denominated in sterling or by reference to allotted share capital denominated in euros (but not partly in one and partly in the other).
Whether the requirement is met is determined in the first case by reference to the sterling amount and in the second case by reference to the prescribed euro equivalent.
No account is to be taken of any allotted share capital of the company denominated in a currency other than sterling or, as the case may be, euros.

If the company could meet the requirement either by reference to share capital denominated in sterling or by reference to share capital denominated in euros, it must elect in its application for a trading certificate or, as the case may be, for re-registration as a public company which is to be the currency by reference to which the matter is determined.

P1group.Title: Authorised minimum: application where shares denominated in different currencies etc

P2para.Text: The Secretary of State may make provision by regulations as to the application of the authorised minimum in relation to a public company that—

Text.Substitution: has shares denominated—
in more than one currency, or
in a currency other than sterling or euros,

P3para.Text: redenominates the whole or part of its allotted share capital, or
allots new shares.

P2para.Text: The regulations may make provision as to the currencies, exchange rates and dates by reference to which it is to be determined whether the nominal value of the company's allotted share capital is less than the authorised minimum.
The regulations may provide that where—

P3para.Text: a company has redenominated the whole or part of its allotted share capital, and
the effect of the redenomination is that the nominal value of the company's allotted share capital is less than the authorised minimum,

P2para.Text: the company must re-register as a private company.
Regulations under subsection (3) may make provision corresponding to any provision made by sections 664 to 667 (re-registration as private company in consequence of cancellation of shares).
Any regulations under this section have effect subject to section 765 (authorised minimum: application of initial requirement).
Regulations under this section are subject to negative resolution procedure.

P1group.Title: Consequences of doing business etc without a trading certificate

P2para.Text: If a company does business or exercises any borrowing powers in contravention of section 761, an offence is committed by—

P3para.Text: the company, and
every officer of the company who is in default.

P2para.Text: A person guilty of an offence under subsection (1) is liable—

P3para.Text: on conviction on indictment, to a fine;
on summary conviction, to a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.

P2para.Text: A contravention of section 761 does not affect the validity of a transaction entered into by the company, but if a company—

P3para.Text: enters into a transaction in contravention of that section, and
fails to comply with its obligations in connection with the transaction within 21 days from being called on to do so,

P2para.Text: the directors of the company are jointly and severally liable to indemnify any other party to the transaction in respect of any loss or damage suffered by him by reason of the company's failure to comply with its obligations.
The directors who are so liable are those who were directors at the time the company entered into the transaction.

Chapter.Title: Certification and transfer of securities: general

P1group.Title: Share certificate to be evidence of title

P2para.Text: In the case of a company registered in England and Wales or Northern Ireland, a certificate under the common seal of the company specifying any shares held by a member is prima facie evidence of his title to the shares.
In the case of a company registered in Scotland—

P3para.Text: a certificate under the common seal of the company specifying any shares held by a member, or
a certificate specifying any shares held by a member and subscribed by the company in accordance with the Requirements of Writing (Scotland) Act 1995 (c. 7),

P2para.Text: is sufficient evidence, unless the contrary is shown, of his title to the shares.

Title.Emphasis: Issue of certificates etc on allotment

P1group.Title: Duty of company as to issue of certificates etc on allotment

P2para.Text: A company must, within two months after the allotment of any of its shares, debentures or debenture stock, complete and have ready for delivery—

P3para.Text: the certificates of the shares allotted,
the debentures allotted, or
the certificates of the debenture stock allotted.

P2para.Text: Subsection (1) does not apply—

P3para.Text: if the conditions of issue of the shares, debentures or debenture stock provide otherwise,
in the case of allotment to a financial institution (see section 778), or
in the case of an allotment of shares if, following the allotment, the company has issued a share warrant in respect of the shares (see section 779).

P2para.Text: If default is made in complying with subsection (1) an offence is committed by every officer of the company who is in default.

A person guilty of an offence under subsection (3) is liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding level 3 on the standard scale and, for continued contravention, a daily default fine not exceeding one-tenth of level 3 on the standard scale.

P1group.Title: Registration of transfer

P2para.Text: A company may not register a transfer of shares in or debentures of the company unless—

P3para.Text: a proper instrument of transfer has been delivered to it, or
the transfer—

P4para.Text: is an exempt transfer within the Stock Transfer Act 1982 (c. 41), or
is in accordance with regulations under Chapter 2 of this Part.

P2para.Text: Subsection (1) does not affect any power of the company to register as shareholder or debenture holder a person to whom the right to any shares in or debentures of the company has been transmitted by operation of law.

P1group.Title: Procedure on transfer being lodged

P2para.Text: When a transfer of shares in or debentures of a company has been lodged with the company, the company must either—

P3para.Text: register the transfer, or
give the transferee notice of refusal to register the transfer, together with its reasons for the refusal,

P2para.Text: as soon as practicable and in any event within two months after the date on which the transfer is lodged with it.

Text.Addition: The company may not register the transfer under subsection (1)(a) unless satisfied that it has the information that it is required to enter in its register of members in relation to the transferee.

P2para.Text: If the company refuses to register the transfer, it must provide the transferee with such further information about the reasons for the refusal as the transferee may reasonably request.
This does not include copies of minutes of meetings of directors.
If a company fails to comply with this section, an offence is committed by—

P3para.Text: the company, and
every officer of the company who is in default.

P2para.Text: A person guilty of an offence under this section is liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding level 3 on the standard scale and, for continued contravention, a daily default fine not exceeding one-tenth of level 3 on the standard scale.
This section does not apply—

P3para.Text: in relation to a transfer of shares if the company has issued a share warrant in respect of the shares (see section 779);
in relation to the transmission of shares or debentures by operation of law.

P1group.Title: Transfer of shares on application of transferor

P1para.Text: On the application of the transferor of any share or interest in a company, the company shall enter in its register of members the name of the transferee ... in the same manner and subject to the same conditions as if the application for the entry ... were made by the transferee.

P1group.Title: Execution of share transfer by personal representative

P1para.Text: An instrument of transfer of the share or other interest of a deceased member of a company—

P3para.Text: may be made by his personal representative although the personal representative is not himself a member of the company, and
is as effective as if the personal representative had been such a member at the time of the execution of the instrument.

P1group.Title: Evidence of grant of probate etc

P1para.Text: The production to a company of any document that is by law sufficient evidence of the grant of—

P3para.Text: probate of the will of a deceased person,
letters of administration of the estate of a deceased person, or
confirmation as executor of a deceased person,

P1para.Text: shall be accepted by the company as sufficient evidence of the grant.

P1group.Title: Certification of instrument of transfer

P2para.Text: The certification by a company of an instrument of transfer of any shares in, or debentures of, the company is to be taken as a representation by the company to any person acting on the faith of the certification that there have been produced to the company such documents as on their face show a prima facie title to the shares or debentures in the transferor named in the instrument.
The certification is not to be taken as a representation that the transferor has any title to the shares or debentures.
Where a person acts on the faith of a false certification by a company made negligently, the company is under the same liability to him as if the certification had been made fraudulently.
For the purposes of this section—

P3para.Text: an instrument of transfer is certificated if it bears the words “certificate lodged” (or words to the like effect);
the certification of an instrument of transfer is made by a company if—

P4para.Text: the person issuing the instrument is a person authorised to issue certificated instruments of transfer on the company's behalf, and
the certification is signed by a person authorised to certificate transfers on the company's behalf or by an officer or employee either of the company or of a body corporate so authorised;

P3para.Text: a certification is treated as signed by a person if—

P4para.Text: it purports to be authenticated by his signature or initials (whether handwritten or not), and

it is not shown that the signature or initials was or were placed there neither by himself nor by a person authorised to use the signature or initials for the purpose of certificating transfers on the company's behalf.

Title.Emphasis: Issue of certificates etc on transfer

P1group.Title: Duty of company as to issue of certificates etc on transfer

P2para.Text: A company must, within two months after the date on which a transfer of any of its shares, debentures or debenture stock is lodged with the company, complete and have ready for delivery—

P3para.Text: the certificates of the shares transferred,
the debentures transferred, or
the certificates of the debenture stock transferred.

P2para.Text: For this purpose a “transfer” means—

P3para.Text: a transfer duly stamped and otherwise valid, or
an exempt transfer within the Stock Transfer Act 1982 (c. 41),

P2para.Text: but does not include a transfer that the company is for any reason entitled to refuse to register and does not register.
Subsection (1) does not apply—

P3para.Text: if the conditions of issue of the shares, debentures or debenture stock provide otherwise,
in the case of a transfer to a financial institution (see section 778), or
in the case of a transfer of shares if, following the transfer, the company has issued a share warrant in respect of the shares (see section 779).

P2para.Text: Subsection (1) has effect subject to section 777 (cases where the Stock Transfer Act 1982 applies).
If default is made in complying with subsection (1) an offence is committed by every officer of the company who is in default.

A person guilty of an offence under this section is liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding level 3 on the standard scale and, for continued contravention, a daily default fine not exceeding one-tenth of level 3 on the standard scale.

P1group.Title: Issue of certificates etc: cases within the Stock Transfer Act 1982

P2para.Text: Section 776(1) (duty of company as to issue of certificates etc on transfer) does not apply in the case of a transfer to a person where, by virtue of regulations under section 3 of the Stock Transfer Act 1982, he is not entitled to a certificate or other document of or evidencing title in respect of the securities transferred.
But if in such a case the transferee—

P3para.Text: subsequently becomes entitled to such a certificate or other document by virtue of any provision of those regulations, and
gives notice in writing of that fact to the company,

P2para.Text: section 776 (duty to company as to issue of certificates etc) has effect as if the reference in subsection (1) of that section to the date of the lodging of the transfer were a reference to the date of the notice.

Title.Emphasis: Issue of certificates etc on allotment or transfer to financial institution

P1group.Title: Issue of certificates etc: allotment or transfer to financial institution

P2para.Text: A company—

P3para.Text: of which shares or debentures are allotted to a financial institution,
of which debenture stock is allotted to a financial institution, or
with which a transfer for transferring shares, debentures or debenture stock to a financial institution is lodged,

P2para.Text: is not required in consequence of that allotment or transfer to comply with section 769(1) or 776(1) (duty of company as to issue of certificates etc).
A “financial institution” means—

P3para.Text: a recognised clearing house or a recognised CSD acting in relation to a recognised investment exchange, or
a nominee of—

P4para.Text: a recognised clearing house or a recognised CSD acting in that way, or
a recognised investment exchange,

P3para.Text: designated for the purposes of this section in the rules of the recognised investment exchange in question.

P2para.Text: Expressions used in subsection (2) have the same meaning as in Part 18 of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (c. 8).

Title.Substitution: Prohibition on issue of new share warrants and effect of existing share warrants

P2para.Text: A company limited by shares may, if so authorised by its articles, issue with respect to any fully paid shares a warrant (a “share warrant”) stating that the bearer of the warrant is entitled to the shares specified in it.

A share warrant issued under the company's common seal or (in the case of a company registered in Scotland) subscribed in accordance with the Requirements of Writing (Scotland) Act 1995 (c. 7) entitles the bearer to the shares specified in it and the shares may be transferred by delivery of the warrant.
A company that issues a share warrant may, if so authorised by its articles, provide (by coupons or otherwise) for the payment of the future dividends on the shares included in the warrant.

Text.Addition: No share warrant may be issued by a company (irrespective of whether its articles purport to authorise it to do so) on or after the day on which section 84 of the Small Business, Enterprise and Employment Act 2015 comes into force.

P1group.Title: Duty of company as to issue of certificates on surrender of share warrant
Offences in connection with share warrants (Scotland)

P2para.Text: If in Scotland a person—

P3para.Text: with intent to defraud, forges or alters, or offers, utters, disposes of, or puts off, knowing the same to be forged or altered, any share warrant or coupon, or any document purporting to be a share warrant or coupon issued in pursuance of this Act, or
by means of any such forged or altered share warrant, coupon or document—

P4para.Text: demands or endeavours to obtain or receive any share or interest in a company under this Act, or
demands or endeavours to receive any dividend or money payment in respect of any such share or interest,

P3para.Text: knowing the warrant, coupon or document to be forged or altered,

P2para.Text: he commits an offence.
If in Scotland a person without lawful authority or excuse (of which proof lies on him)—

P3para.Text: engraves or makes on any plate, wood, stone, or other material, any share warrant or coupon purporting to be—

P4para.Text: a share warrant or coupon issued or made by any particular company in pursuance of this Act, or
a blank share warrant or coupon so issued or made, or
a part of such a share warrant or coupon, or

P3para.Text: uses any such plate, wood, stone, or other material, for the making or printing of any such share warrant or coupon, or of any such blank share warrant or coupon or of any part of such a share warrant or coupon, or
knowingly has in his custody or possession any such plate, wood, stone, or other material,

P2para.Text: he commits an offence.

A person guilty of an offence under subsection (1) is liable on summary conviction to imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months or to a fine not exceeding level 5 on the standard scale (or both).
A person guilty of an offence under subsection (2) is liable—

P3para.Text: on conviction on indictment, to imprisonment for a term not exceeding seven years or a fine (or both);
on summary conviction, to imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum (or both).

P1group.Title: Issue of certificates etc: court order to make good default

P2para.Text: If a company on which a notice has been served requiring it to make good any default in complying with—

P3para.Text: section 769(1) (duty of company as to issue of certificates etc on allotment),
section 776(1) (duty of company as to issue of certificates etc on transfer), or
section 780(1) (duty of company as to issue of certificates etc on surrender of share warrant),

P2para.Text: fails to make good the default within ten days after service of the notice, the person entitled to have the certificates or the debentures delivered to him may apply to the court.
The court may on such an application make an order directing the company and any officer of it to make good the default within such time as may be specified in the order.
The order may provide that all costs (in Scotland, expenses) of and incidental to the application are to be borne by the company or by an officer of it responsible for the default.

Chapter.Title: Evidencing and transfer of title to securities without written instrument

P1group.Title: Scope of this Chapter

P1para.Text: In this Chapter—

P3para.Text: “securities” means shares, debentures, debenture stock, loan stock, bonds, units of a collective investment scheme within the meaning of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (c. 8) and other securities of any description;
references to title to securities include any legal or equitable interest in securities;
references to a transfer of title include a transfer by way of security;
references to transfer without a written instrument include, in relation to bearer securities, transfer without delivery.

P1group.Title: Power to make regulations

P2para.Text: The power to make regulations under this Chapter is exercisable by the Treasury and the Secretary of State, either jointly or concurrently.
References in this Chapter to the authority having power to make regulations shall accordingly be read as references to both or either of them, as the case may require.
Regulations under this Chapter are subject to affirmative resolution procedure.

P1group.Title: Provision enabling procedures for evidencing and transferring title

P2para.Text: Provision may be made by regulations for enabling title to securities to be evidenced and transferred without a written instrument.
The regulations may make provision—

P3para.Text: for procedures for recording and transferring title to securities, and
for the regulation of those procedures and the persons responsible for or involved in their operation.

P2para.Text: The regulations must contain such safeguards as appear to the authority making the regulations appropriate for the protection of investors and for ensuring that competition is not restricted, distorted or prevented.

The regulations may, for the purpose of enabling or facilitating the operation of the procedures provided for by the regulations, make provision with respect to the rights and obligations of persons in relation to securities dealt with under the procedures.
The regulations may include provision for the purpose of giving effect to—

P3para.Text: the transmission of title to securities by operation of law;
any restriction on the transfer of title to securities arising by virtue of the provisions of any enactment or instrument, court order or agreement;
any power conferred by any such provision on a person to deal with securities on behalf of the person entitled.

P2para.Text: The regulations may make provision with respect to the persons responsible for the operation of the procedures provided for by the regulations—

P3para.Text: as to the consequences of their insolvency or incapacity, or
as to the transfer from them to other persons of their functions in relation to those procedures.

Text.Addition: The regulations may confer functions on any person, including—
the function of giving guidance or issuing a code of practice in relation to any provision made by the regulations, and
the function of making rules for the purposes of any provision made by the regulations.
The regulations may, in prescribed cases, confer immunity from liability in damages.

P1group.Title: Provision enabling or requiring arrangements to be adopted

P2para.Text: Regulations under this Chapter may make provision—

P3para.Text: enabling the members of a company or of any designated class of companies to adopt, by ordinary resolution, arrangements under which title to securities is required to be evidenced or transferred (or both) without a written instrument; or
requiring companies, or any designated class of companies, to adopt such arrangements.

P2para.Text: The regulations may make such provision—

P3para.Text: in respect of all securities issued by a company, or
in respect of all securities of a specified description.

P2para.Text: The arrangements provided for by regulations making such provision as is mentioned in subsection (1)—

P3para.Text: must not be such that a person who but for the arrangements would be entitled to have his name entered in the company's register of members ... ceases to be so entitled, and
must be such that a person who but for the arrangements would be entitled to exercise any rights in respect of the securities continues to be able effectively to control the exercise of those rights.

P2para.Text: The regulations may—

P3para.Text: prohibit the issue of any certificate by the company in respect of the issue or transfer of securities,
require the provision by the company to holders of securities of statements (at specified intervals or on specified occasions) of the securities held in their name, and
make provision as to the matters of which any such certificate or statement is, or is not, evidence.

P2para.Text: In this section—

P3para.Text: references to a designated class of companies are to a class designated in the regulations or by order under section 787; and
“specified” means specified in the regulations.

P1group.Title: Provision enabling or requiring arrangements to be adopted: order-making powers

P2para.Text: The authority having power to make regulations under this Chapter may by order—

P3para.Text: designate classes of companies for the purposes of section 786 (provision enabling or requiring arrangements to be adopted);
provide that, in relation to securities of a specified description—

P4para.Text: in a designated class of companies, or
in a specified company or class of companies,

P3para.Text: specified provisions of regulations made under this Chapter by virtue of that section either do not apply or apply subject to specified modifications.

P2para.Text: In subsection (1) “specified” means specified in the order.
An order under this section is subject to negative resolution procedure.

P1group.Title: Provision that may be included in regulations

P1para.Text: Regulations under this Chapter may—

P3para.Text: modify or exclude any provision of any enactment or instrument, or any rule of law;
apply, with such modifications as may be appropriate, the provisions of any enactment or instrument (including provisions creating criminal offences);
require the payment of fees, or enable persons to require the payment of fees, of such amounts as may be specified in the regulations or determined in accordance with them;
empower the authority making the regulations to delegate to any person willing and able to discharge them any functions of the authority under the regulations.

P1group.Title: Duty to consult

P1para.Text: Before making—

P3para.Text: regulations under this Chapter, or
any order under section 787,

P1para.Text: the authority having power to make regulations under this Chapter must carry out such consultation as appears to it to be appropriate.

P1group.Title: Resolutions to be forwarded to registrar

P1para.Text: Chapter 3 of Part 3 (resolutions affecting a company's constitution) applies to a resolution passed by virtue of regulations under this Chapter.

Title.Addition: Information about people with significant control
Introduction
Overview

Text.Addition: This Part is arranged as follows—
the remaining provisions of this Chapter identify the companies to which this Part applies and explain some key terms, including what it means to have “significant control” over a company,
Chapter 2 imposes duties on companies to gather information, and on others to supply information, to enable companies to

Addition.Addition: notify the registrar of the information in accordance with Chapter 2A
Chapter 2A requires companies to notify the registrar of information relating to persons with significant control;

Text.Addition: Chapter 5 makes provision for excluding certain material from the information available to the public.

Title.Addition: Companies to which this Part applies

Text.Addition: This Part applies to companies other than—

Addition.Substitution: companies with voting shares admitted to trading on a

Substitution.Substitution: UK regulated market or an EU regulated market

Text.Addition: companies of any description specified by the Secretary of State by regulations.

In deciding whether to specify a description of company, the Secretary of State is to have regard to the extent to which companies of that description are bound by disclosure and transparency rules (in the United Kingdom or elsewhere)

Addition.Substitution: which are contained in international standards and are equivalent to those applicable to companies referred to in subsection (1)(a)

Text.Addition: Regulations under this section are subject to affirmative resolution procedure.

Addition.Addition: “voting shares” means shares carrying voting rights;
“voting rights” means rights to vote at general meetings of the company in question, including rights that arise only in certain circumstances.

Title.Addition: Key terms

Text.Addition: This section explains some key terms used in this Part.
References to a person with (or having) “significant control” over a company are to an individual who meets one or more of the specified conditions in relation to the company.
The “specified conditions” are those specified in Part 1 of Schedule 1A.
Individuals with significant control over a company are either “registrable” or “
” in relation to the company—

Addition.Substitution: they are “non-registrable” if they do not hold any interest in the company except through one or more legal entities over each of which they have significant control and—

as respects any shares or right in the company which they hold indirectly as described in paragraph 9(1)(b)(i) of Schedule 1A, the legal entity through which the shares or right are held is a relevant legal entity in relation to the company; and

as respects any shares or right in the company which they hold indirectly as described in paragraph 9(1)(b)(ii) of Schedule 1A, at least one of the legal entities in the chain is a relevant legal entity in relation to the company

Text.Addition: otherwise, they are “registrable”,
and references to a “
” in relation to a company are to an individual with significant control over the company who is registrable in relation to that company.
A “legal entity” is a body corporate or a firm that is a legal person under the law by which it is governed.
In relation to a company, a legal entity is a “relevant legal entity” if—
it would have come within the definition of a person with significant control over the company if it had been an individual, and
it is subject to its own disclosure requirements.
A legal entity is “subject to its own disclosure requirements” if—
this Part applies to it (whether by virtue of section 790B or another enactment that extends the application of this Part),

Addition.Addition: it is an eligible Scottish partnership within the meaning of regulation 3(2) of the Scottish Partnerships (Register of People with Significant Control) Regulations 2017.

Addition.Substitution: it has voting shares admitted to trading on a

Substitution.Substitution: UK regulated market or an EU regulated market,

Text.Addition: it is of a description specified in regulations under section 790B (or that section as extended), or
it is of a description specified by the Secretary of State by regulations made under this paragraph.
A relevant legal entity is either “registrable” or “
” in relation to a company—

Addition.Substitution: it is “non-registrable” if it does not hold any interest in the company except through one or more other legal entities over each of which it has significant control and—

as respects any shares or right in the company which it holds indirectly as described in paragraph 9(1)(b)(i) of Schedule 1A, the legal entity through which the shares or right are held is also a relevant legal entity in relation to the company; and

as respects any shares or right in the company which it holds indirectly as described in paragraph 9(1)(b)(ii) of Schedule 1A, at least one of the legal entities in the chain is also a relevant legal entity in relation to the company;

Text.Addition: otherwise, it is “registrable”,
and references to a “
” in relation to a company are to a relevant legal entity which is registrable in relation to that company.
For the purposes of subsections (4) and (8)—
whether someone—
holds an interest in a company, or
holds that interest through another legal entity,
is to be determined in accordance with Part 2 of Schedule 1A;

whether someone has significant control over that other legal entity is to be determined in accordance with subsections (2) and (3) and Part 1 of Schedule 1A, reading references in those provisions to the company as references to that other entity.

In deciding whether to specify a description of legal entity under paragraph (d) of subsection (7), the Secretary of State is to have regard to the extent to which entities of that description are bound by disclosure and transparency rules (in the United Kingdom or elsewhere)
to the ones applying to an entity falling within any other paragraph of that subsection.

Subject to express provision in this Part and to any modification prescribed by regulations under this subsection, this Part is to be read and have effect as if each of the following were an individual, even if they are legal persons under the laws by which they are governed—
a corporation sole,
a government or government department of a country or territory or a part of a country or territory,
an international organisation whose members include two or more countries or territories (or their governments),
a local authority or local government body in the United Kingdom or elsewhere.
Regulations under subsection (7)(d) are subject to affirmative resolution procedure.
Subject to subsection (13), regulations under this section are subject to negative resolution procedure.

Addition.Addition: In this section “voting shares” has the same meaning as in section 790B.
For the purposes of this Part a company has had confirmation of—
a person’s status as a registrable person or a registrable relevant legal entity in relation to the company,
the required particulars of a person (see section 790K), or
any other information about a person,

if the person has supplied that information to the company whether or not in pursuance of any duty imposed by this Part (and references to a company obtaining confirmation of information are to be read accordingly).

Title.Addition: Information-gathering

Addition.Addition: Duty to find out about persons with significant control

A company to which this Part applies must take reasonable steps to find out if there is anyone who is a registrable person or a registrable relevant legal entity in relation to the company and, if so, to identify them.
Company’s duty to give notices to persons with significant control
A company to which this Part applies must give a notice to a person under this section if—
the company knows or has cause to believe that the person is a registrable person or a registrable relevant legal entity in relation to the company, but

the company has not had confirmation of the person’s status as a registrable person or registrable relevant legal entity or has not had confirmation of all of the required particulars of the person (see section 790K).
The notice must require the person—
to inform the company whether the person is a registrable person or a registrable relevant legal entity in relation to the company, and
if they are, to give the company all of the required particulars of the person (see section 790K).
The notice must require the person to whom it is given to comply with the notice by no later than the end of the period of one month beginning with the day on which it is given.
The company must give the notice—
as soon as reasonably practicable after the company becomes subject to the duty to give a notice under this section, and
in any event before the end of the period of 14 days beginning with the day on which the company becomes so subject.
A company is not required to give a notice under this section to a person if—

the application for the registration of the company contained a statement of initial significant control naming the person as someone who would, on the company’s incorporation, become a registrable person or a registrable relevant legal entity in relation to the company, and
the company has no cause to believe that at any time since its incorporation the person has ceased to be a registrable person or a registrable relevant legal entity in relation to the company.

The Secretary of State may by regulations make further provision about the giving of notices under this section, including provision about their form and content and the manner in which they must be given.
Regulations under subsection (6) are subject to negative resolution procedure.
A company to which this Part applies may give a notice to a person under this section if it knows or has cause to believe that the person—
knows the identity of someone who falls within subsection (2), or
knows the identity of someone likely to have that knowledge.
The persons who fall within this subsection are—
a registrable person in relation to the company;
a relevant legal entity in relation to the company;
an entity which would be a relevant legal entity in relation to the company but for the fact that section 790C(6)(b) does not apply in respect of it.
A company must give a notice under subsection (1) to a person (“a third party”) if the company—
knows or has cause to believe that a person is a registrable person or a registrable relevant legal entity in relation to the company (“a suspected PSC”),
is under a duty to give the suspected PSC a notice under section 790D but does not have the information that it needs in order to contact them, and
knows or has cause to believe that the third party—
knows the identity of the suspected PSC, or
knows the identity of someone likely to have that knowledge.
A notice under subsection (1) must require the person to whom it is given (“
to inform the company whether the recipient knows the identity of any person who—
is likely to know the identity of anyone who falls within subsection (2), and
if the recipient does, to give the company any information within the recipient’s knowledge that would allow the company to contact each such person.
The notice must require the person to whom it is given to comply with the notice by no later than the end of the period of one month beginning with the day on which it is given.

A person to whom a notice under subsection (1) is given is not required by that notice to disclose any information in respect of which a claim to legal professional privilege (in Scotland, to confidentiality of communications) could be maintained in legal proceedings.

The Secretary of State may by regulations make further provision about the giving of notices under this section, including provision about their form and content and the manner in which they must be given.
Regulations under subsection (7) are subject to negative resolution procedure.
In this section a reference to knowing the identity of a person includes knowing information from which that person can be identified.
Company’s duty to find out about changes in PSC information
This section applies if a company—

knows or has cause to believe that there has been a change in the required particulars of a registrable person or a registrable relevant legal entity in relation to the company (see section 790K), but

has not had confirmation that the change has occurred or has not had confirmation of all of the information that the company would need to include in a notice of the change under section 790LD(1) or 790LE(1).
The company must give the person a notice requiring the person—
to inform the company whether the change has occurred, and
if it has, to give the company the information that the company would need to include in a notice of the change under section 790LD(1) or 790LE(1).
The notice must require the person to whom it is given to comply with the notice by no later than the end of the period of one month beginning with the day on which it is given.
The company must give the notice—
as soon as reasonably practicable after the company becomes subject to the duty to give a notice under subsection (2), and
in any event before the end of the period of 14 days beginning with the day on which the company becomes so subject.

The Secretary of State may by regulations make further provision about the giving of notices under this section, including provision about their form and content and the manner in which they must be given.
Regulations under subsection (5) are subject to negative resolution procedure.
Company’s duty to find out about persons ceasing to be PSCs
This section applies if a company —
knows or has cause to believe that a person has ceased to be a registrable person or a registrable relevant legal entity in relation to the company, but

has not had confirmation that the person has ceased to be a registrable person or a registrable relevant legal entity in relation to the company or has not had confirmation of the date on which the person so ceased.
The company must give the person a notice requiring the person—
to inform the company whether the person has ceased to be a registrable person or a registrable relevant legal entity in relation to the company, and
if the person has, to inform the company of the date on which the person so ceased.
The notice must require the person to whom it is given to comply with the notice by no later than the end of the period of one month beginning with the day on which it is given.
The company must give the notice—
as soon as reasonably practicable after the company becomes subject to the duty under subsection (2), and
in any event before the end of the period of 14 days beginning with the day on which the company becomes so subject.

The Secretary of State may by regulations make further provision about the giving of notices under this section, including provision about their form and content and the manner in which they must be given.
Regulations under subsection (5) are subject to negative resolution procedure.
Company’s duty to notify failure to comply with notices
A company must notify the registrar if a person fails to comply with a notice given by the company under section 790D, 790DA, 790E or 790EA within the period specified in it.
The notice must state the day on which the period mentioned in subsection (1) ends.
Where a company notifies the registrar that a person has failed to comply with a notice given by the company under section 790E or 790EA, the notice must state the person’s name.
The notice must be given within the period of 14 days beginning with the end of the period specified in the notice under section 790D, 790DA, 790E or 790EA.
”, in relation to an individual, means their forename and surname.
Company’s duty to notify of late compliance with notices

A company must notify the registrar if a person who has failed to comply with a notice given by the company under section 790D, 790DA, 790E or 790EA within the period specified in it subsequently complies.
The notice must state the day on which the person complied.
Where a company notifies the registrar in relation to the late compliance by a person with a notice given by the company under section 790E or 790EA, the notice must state the person’s name.
The notice must be given within the period of 14 days beginning with the day on which the person complied with the notice under section 790D, 790DA, 790E or 790EA.
”, in relation to an individual, means their forename and surname.
Company’s duty to notify that it has given a restrictions notice
A company that has issued a restrictions notice under paragraph 1(3) of Schedule 1B must notify the registrar.
The notice must state the date on which the restrictions notice was given.
The notice must be given within the period of 14 days beginning with the day on which the restrictions notice was given.
” has the meaning given in paragraph 1(2) of Schedule 1B.
Company’s duty to notify that it has withdrawn a restrictions notice
A company that has given a withdrawal notice must notify the registrar.
The notice must state the date on which the withdrawal notice was given.
The notice must be given within the period of 14 days beginning with the day on which the withdrawal notice was given.
” means a notice given by a company under paragraph 11 of Schedule 1B.
Company’s duty to notify that court has ended restrictions

Where a court makes an order under paragraph 8 of Schedule 1B directing that a relevant interest in a company cease to be subject to restrictions set out in a restrictions notice given by the company, the company must give notice to the registrar.
that the court has made an order under paragraph 8 of Schedule 1B directing that a relevant interest in the company cease to be subject to restrictions in a restrictions notice, and
The notice must be given within the period of 14 days beginning with the day on which the company is made aware of the court’s order.

Title.Addition: Failure by company to comply with information duties

Addition.Addition: If a company fails, without reasonable excuse, to comply with a duty under section 790CB, 790D, 790DA(3), 790E, 790EA,
to take steps or give a notice, an offence is committed by—
every officer of the company who is in default.

Text.Addition: A person guilty of an offence under this section is liable—
on conviction on indictment, to imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years or a fine (or both);
on summary conviction—
in England and Wales, to imprisonment for a term not exceeding twelve months or a fine (or both);
in Scotland, to imprisonment for a term not exceeding twelve months or to a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum (or both);
in Northern Ireland, to imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months or to a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum (or both).

Addition.Addition: Duty to notify company on becoming PSC
This section applies to a person if—
the person knows that they are a registrable person or a registrable relevant legal entity in relation to a company,
the material in the register that is available for public inspection does not indicate the person’s status as a registrable person or registrable relevant legal entity in relation to the company, and
has not informed the company of the person’s status as a registrable person or registrable relevant legal entity in relation to the company, or
has not given the company all of the required particulars of the person (see section 790K).
inform the company of the person’s status as a registrable person or registrable relevant legal entity in relation to the company, and
give the company the required particulars (see section 790K).
The person must comply with the duty in subsection (2) before the end of the period of one month beginning with the day on which the conditions in subsection (1) are met.
Duty to notify company of changes in PSC information
This section applies to a person if—
the person knows that they are a registrable person or a registrable relevant legal entity in relation to a company,
there has been a change in the required particulars of the person (see section 790K) and the person knows that to be the case, and

the person has not informed the company of the change or has not given the company all of the information that the company would need to include in a notice of the change under section 790LD(1) or 790LE(1).
inform the company of the change, and
give the company the information that the company would need to include in a notice of the change under section 790LD(1) or 790LE(1).
The person must comply with the duty in subsection (2) before the end of the period of one month beginning with the day on which the conditions in subsection (1) are met.
Duty to notify company of ceasing to be a PSC
This section applies to a person if—
the person knows that they have ceased to be a registrable person or a registrable relevant legal entity in relation to a company,

the material in the register that is available for public inspection does not indicate the person as having ceased to be a registrable person or a registrable relevant legal entity in relation to a company, and

the person has not informed the company of having ceased to be a registrable person or a registrable relevant legal entity in relation to the company or has not informed the company of the date on which the person so ceased.
The person must inform the company—
that the person has ceased to be a registrable person or a registrable relevant legal entity in relation to the company, and
of the date on which the person so ceased.
The person must comply with the duty in subsection (2) before the end of the period of one month beginning with the day on which the conditions in subsection (1) are met.

Title.Addition: Enforcement of disclosure requirements

Text.Addition: Schedule 1B contains provisions for when a person (whether an individual or a legal entity) fails to comply with

Addition.Addition: a notice under section 790D, 790DA, 790E or 790EA, or
Power to impose further duties involving nominee shareholders

The Secretary of State may by regulations make further provision for the purpose of enabling a company to which this Part applies to find out about anyone who has become or ceased to be a person who is—
a registrable person in relation to the company by virtue of shares being held by a nominee, or
a registrable relevant legal entity in relation to the company by virtue of shares being held by a nominee.
impose obligations on a company with a view to obtaining—
information about whether a person has become or ceased to be a nominee shareholder;
if they have, information about: (A) the shareholding; (B) the nominee; (C) the person for whom the nominee holds or held the shares;
any other information required by the regulations;
impose obligations on others (including nominees or former nominees) with a view to providing the company with—
information of a kind described in paragraph (a)(i) or (ii);
any other information required by the regulations.
The regulations may, in particular, make provision similar or corresponding to any of the preceding provisions of this Chapter.
The provision that may be made by regulations under subsection (1) includes provision amending this Chapter.
Regulations under this section are subject to affirmative resolution procedure.

Emphasis.Addition: Exemption from information and registration requirements

Title.Addition: Power to make exemptions

Text.Addition: The Secretary of State may exempt a person (whether an individual or a legal entity) under this section.
The effect of an exemption is—
the person is not required to comply with any notice under section
(but if a notice is received, the person must bring the existence of the exemption to the attention of the company that sent it),
companies are not obliged to take steps or give notice under those sections to or with respect to that person,
notices under section
do not require anyone else to give any information about that person,
the duties imposed by sections 790G
do not apply to that person, and
the person does not count for the purposes of
as a registrable person or, as the case may be, a registrable relevant legal entity in relation to any company.

The Secretary of State must not grant an exemption under this section unless the Secretary of State is satisfied that, having regard to any undertaking given by the person to be exempted, there are special reasons why that person should be exempted.

Title.Addition: Required particulars

Text.Addition: The “required particulars” of an individual who is a registrable person are—
name,
a service address,
the country or state (or part of the United Kingdom) in which the individual is usually resident,
nationality,
date of birth,
usual residential address,
the date on which the individual became a registrable person in relation to the company in question,
the nature of his or her control over that company (see Schedule 1A),
In the case of a person in relation to which this Part has effect by virtue of section 790C(12) as if the person were an individual, the “required particulars” are—
name,
principal office,
the legal form of the person and the law by which it is governed,
the date on which it became a registrable person in relation to the company in question, and
the nature of its control over the company (see Schedule 1A).
The “required particulars” of a registrable relevant legal entity are—
corporate or firm name,
... principal office,
the legal form of the entity and the law by which it is governed,
if applicable, the register of companies in which it is entered (including details of the state) and its registration number in that register,
the date on which it became a registrable relevant legal entity in relation to the company in question, and
the nature of its control over that company (see Schedule 1A).

Addition.Addition: ”, in relation to an individual, means the individual’s forename and surname.

Where an individual is a peer or an individual usually known by a title, any requirement imposed by this Act to provide the individual’s name because it forms part of the required particulars under this section may be satisfied by providing that title instead of the individual’s forename and surname.

Text.Addition: The Secretary of State may by regulations make further provision about the particulars required by subsections (1)(h), (2)(e) and (3)(f).
Regulations under subsection (5) are subject to negative resolution procedure.

Title.Addition: Required particulars: power to amend

Addition.Addition: The Secretary of State may by regulations—
amend section 790K so as to change the “
an individual who is a registrable person;
a person in relation to which this Part has effect by virtue of section 790C(12) as if the person were an individual;

Text.Addition: Regulations under this section are subject to affirmative resolution procedure.

Addition.Addition: Duty to notify registrar of persons with significant control and ID verification
Duty to notify registrar of persons with significant control
Duty to notify registrar of confirmed persons with significant control
A company must give a notice to the registrar if it has had confirmation of—
a person’s status as a registrable person or a registrable relevant legal entity in relation to the company, and
the required particulars of the person (see section 790K).

Addition.Substitution: contain a statement of the required particulars, and
state the date on which the company had confirmation as mentioned in that subsection.

Addition.Addition: A notice under subsection (1) must be given within the period of 14 days beginning with the day on which the company had confirmation as mentioned in that subsection.
A company is not required to give a notice under this section in relation to a person if—

the application for the registration of the company contained a statement of initial significant control naming the person as someone who would, on the company’s incorporation, become a registrable person or a registrable relevant legal entity in relation to the company, and
the company has no cause to believe that at any time since its incorporation the person has ceased to be a registrable person or a registrable relevant legal entity in relation to the company.
Nothing in section 126 (notice of trusts not receivable by registrar) affects the duty to give a notice under this section (or the receipt of that notice by the registrar).
Option to provide ID verification information in notice of change
A notice under section 790LA(1) that relates to a registrable person may include a statement that the person’s identity is verified (see section 1110A).
A notice under section 790LA(1) that relates to a registrable relevant legal entity may include a statement that—
specifies the name of one of its relevant officers (within the meaning given by section 790LO(6)) who is an individual and whose identity is verified, and
confirms that the individual’s identity is verified.

If the notice includes a statement under subsection (2), it must be accompanied by a statement by the individual confirming that the individual is a relevant officer of the registrable relevant legal entity.
To find out what happens if the option in subsection (1) or (2) is not exercised, see sections 790LM and 790LO.
” does not include a person mentioned in section 790C(12)(a) to (d).
Duty to notify registrar of unconfirmed persons with significant control
A company must give a notice to the registrar if—
