The first condition is that the scheme provides that every other holder of relevant securities has the right to require the transferee company to acquire those securities.
The second condition is that, if a holder of securities exercises that right, the consideration to be given for those securities is fair and reasonable.
The powers of the court under section 900(2)

Addition.Addition: or, as the case may be, section 901J(2)

Text.Addition: (power to facilitate reconstruction or amalgamation) include the power to determine, or make provision for the determination of, the consideration to be given for securities acquired under this section.
In this section—
” means a person who holds securities of the transferor company otherwise than on behalf of the transferee company (and does not include the transferee company itself);
”, in relation to a company, means shares or other securities carrying the right to vote at general meetings of the company.

P1group.Title: Circumstances in which meeting of members of transferee company not required (merger)

P2para.Text: This section applies in the case of a merger by absorption where 90% or more (but not all) of the relevant securities of the transferor company (or, if there is more than one transferor company, of each of them) are held by or on behalf of the transferee company.

It is not necessary for the scheme to be approved at a meeting of the members, or any class of members, of the transferee company if the court is satisfied that the following conditions have been complied with.

Text.Substitution: The first condition is that either subsection (3A) or subsection (3B) is satisfied.

This subsection is satisfied if publication of notice of receipt of the draft terms by the registrar took place in respect of the transferee company at least one month before the date of the first meeting of members, or any class of members, of the transferor company summoned for the purpose of agreeing to the scheme.
This subsection is satisfied if—
the conditions in section 906A(2) to (4) are met in respect of the transferee company,

the registrar published the notice mentioned in subsection (4) of that section in the Gazette at least one month before the date of the first meeting of members, or any class of members, of the transferor company summoned for the purpose of agreeing to the scheme, and
the draft terms remained available on the website throughout the period beginning one month before, and ending on, that date.

The second condition is that subsection (4A) or (4B) is satisfied for each of the documents listed in the applicable paragraphs of section 911(3)(a) to (f) relating to the transferee company and the transferor company (or, if there is more than one transferor company, each of them).

This subsection is satisfied for a document if the members of the transferee company were able during the period beginning one month before, and ending on, the date mentioned in subsection (3A) to inspect that document at the registered office of that company.
This subsection is satisfied for a document if—
the document is made available on a website which is maintained by or on behalf of the transferee company and identifies the company,
access to the document on the website is not conditional on the payment of a fee or otherwise restricted, and
the document remains available on the website throughout the period beginning one month before, and ending on, the date mentioned in subsection (3A).

The third condition is that the members of the transferee company were able to obtain copies of the documents mentioned in subsection (4), or any part of those documents, on request and free of charge, throughout the period beginning one month before, and ending on, the date mentioned in subsection (3A).
For the purposes of subsection (4C)—
section 911A(5) applies as it applies for the purposes of section 911(1)(b), and
Part 4 of Schedule 5 (communications by means of a website) does not apply.

P2para.Text: The fourth condition is that—

P3para.Text: one or more members of the transferee company, who together held not less than 5% of the paid-up capital of the company which carried the right to vote at general meetings of the company (excluding any shares in the company held as treasury shares) would have been able, during that period, to require a meeting of each class of members to be called for the purpose of deciding whether or not to agree to the scheme, and
no such requirement was made.

P2para.Text: In this section “relevant securities”, in relation to a company, means shares or other securities carrying the right to vote at general meetings of the company.

P1group.Title: Circumstances in which no meetings required (merger)

P2para.Text: This section applies in the case of a merger by absorption where all of the relevant securities of the transferor company (or, if there is more than one transferor company, of each of them) are held by or on behalf of the transferee company.

It is not necessary for the scheme to be approved at a meeting of the members, or any class of members, of any of the merging companies if the court is satisfied that the following conditions have been complied with.

Text.Substitution: The first condition is that either subsection (3A) or subsection (3B) is satisfied.

This subsection is satisfied if publication of notice of receipt of the draft terms by the registrar took place in respect of all the merging companies at least one month before the date of the court's order.
This subsection is satisfied if—
the conditions in section 906A(2) to (4) are met in respect of each of the merging companies,
in each case, the registrar published the notice mentioned in subsection (4) of that section in the Gazette at least one month before the date of the court's order, and
the draft terms remained available on the website throughout the period beginning one month before, and ending on, that date.

The second condition is that subsection (4A) or (4B) is satisfied for each of the documents listed in the applicable paragraphs of section 911(3)(a) to (f) relating to the transferee company and the transferor company (or, if there is more than one transferor company, each of them).

This subsection is satisfied for a document if the members of the transferee company were able during the period beginning one month before, and ending on, the date mentioned in subsection (3A) to inspect that document at the registered office of that company.
This subsection is satisfied for a document if—
the document is made available on a website which is maintained by or on behalf of the transferee company and identifies the company,
access to the document on the website is not conditional on the payment of a fee or otherwise restricted, and
the document remains available on the website throughout the period beginning one month before, and ending on, the date mentioned in subsection (3A).

The third condition is that the members of the transferee company were able to obtain copies of the documents mentioned in subsection (4), or any part of those documents, on request and free of charge, throughout the period beginning one month before, and ending on, the date mentioned in subsection (3A).
For the purposes of subsection (4C)—
section 911A(5) applies as it applies for the purposes of section 911(1)(b), and
Part 4 of Schedule 5 (communications by means of a website) does not apply.

P2para.Text: The fourth condition is that—

P3para.Text: one or more members of the transferee company, who together held not less than 5% of the paid-up capital of the company which carried the right to vote at general meetings of the company (excluding any shares in the company held as treasury shares) would have been able, during that period, to require a meeting of each class of members to be called for the purpose of deciding whether or not to agree to the scheme, and
no such requirement was made.

P2para.Text: In this section “relevant securities”, in relation to a company, means shares or other securities carrying the right to vote at general meetings of the company.

Title.Addition: Other circumstances in which meeting of members of transferor company not required (merger)

Text.Addition: In the case of a compromise or arrangement to be sanctioned under Part 26A, it is not necessary for the scheme to be approved by the members of the company in respect of which the compromise or arrangement is proposed.

P1group.Title: Other circumstances in which meeting of members of transferee company not required (merger)

P2para.Text: In the case of any merger by absorption, it is not necessary for the scheme to be approved by the members of the transferee company if the court is satisfied that the following conditions have been complied with.

Text.Substitution: The first condition is that either subsection (2A) or subsection (2B) is satisfied.

This subsection is satisfied if publication of notice of receipt of the draft terms by the registrar took place in respect of the transferee company at least one month before the date of the first meeting of members, or any class of members, of the transferor company (or, if there is more than one transferor company, any of them) summoned for the purposes of agreeing to the scheme.
This subsection is satisfied if—
the conditions in section 906A(2) to (4) are met in respect of the transferee company,

the registrar published the notice mentioned in subsection (4) of that section in the Gazette at least one month before the date of the first meeting of members, or any class of members, of the transferor company (or, if there is more than one transferor company, any of them) summoned for the purposes of agreeing to the scheme, and
the draft terms remained available on the website throughout the period beginning one month before, and ending on, that date.

The second condition is that subsection (3A) or (3B) is satisfied for each of the documents listed in the applicable paragraphs of section 911(3) relating to the transferee company and the transferor company (or, if there is more than one transferor company, each of them).

This subsection is satisfied for a document if the members of the transferee company were able during the period beginning one month before, and ending on, the date of any such meeting as is mentioned in subsection (2A) to inspect that document at the registered office of that company.
This subsection is satisfied for a document if—
the document is made available on a website which is maintained by or on behalf of the transferee company and identifies the company,
access to the document on the website is not conditional on the payment of a fee or otherwise restricted, and
the document remains available on the website throughout the period beginning one month before, and ending on, the date of any such meeting as is mentioned in subsection (2A).

The third condition is that the members of the transferee company were able to obtain copies of the documents mentioned in subsection (3), or any part of those documents, on request and free of charge, throughout the period beginning one month before, and ending on, the date of any such meeting as is mentioned in subsection (2A).
For the purposes of subsection (3C)—
section 911A(5) applies as it applies for the purposes of section 911(1)(b), and
Part 4 of Schedule 5 (communications by means of a website) does not apply.

P2para.Text: The fourth condition is that—

P3para.Text: one or more members of that company, who together held not less than 5% of the paid-up capital of the company which carried the right to vote at general meetings of the company (excluding any shares in the company held as treasury shares) would have been able, during that period, to require a meeting of each class of members to be called for the purpose of deciding whether or not to agree to the scheme, and
no such requirement was made.

Title.Addition: Agreement to dispense with
(merger)

Text.Addition: If all members holding shares in, and all persons holding other securities of,
, being shares or securities that carry a right to vote in general meetings of the company in question, so agree,

Addition.Substitution: the following requirements do not apply

Addition.Addition: The requirements that may be dispensed with under this section are—
section 911B (report on material changes of assets of merging company); and
the requirements of section 911 (inspection of documents) so far as relating to any document required to be drawn up under sections 908, 909 or 910.

Text.Addition: For the purposes of this section—
the members, or holders of other securities, of a company, and
whether shares or other securities carry a right to vote in general meetings of the company,
are determined as at the date of
In subsection (2) “the relevant application” means—
in the case of a compromise or arrangement to be sanctioned under Part 26, the application to the court under section 896;
in the case of a compromise or arrangement to be sanctioned under Part 26A, the application to the court under section 901C(1).

P1group.Title: Divisions and companies involved in a division

P2para.Text: The scheme involves a division where under the scheme the undertaking, property and liabilities of the company in respect of which the compromise or arrangement is proposed are to be divided among and transferred to two or more companies each of which is either—

P3para.Text: an existing public company, or
a new company (whether or not a public company).

P2para.Text: References in this Part to the companies involved in the division are to the transferor company and any existing transferee companies.

Title.Emphasis: Requirements to be complied with in case of division

P1group.Title: Draft terms of scheme (division)

P2para.Text: A draft of the proposed terms of the scheme must be drawn up and adopted by the directors of each of the companies involved in the division.
The draft terms must give particulars of at least the following matters—

P3para.Text: in respect of the transferor company and each transferee company—

P4para.Text: its name,
the address of its registered office, and
whether it is a company limited by shares or a company limited by guarantee and having a share capital;

P3para.Text: the number of shares in a transferee company to be allotted to members of the transferor company for a given number of their shares (the “share exchange ratio”) and the amount of any cash payment;
the terms relating to the allotment of shares in a transferee company;
the date from which the holding of shares in a transferee company will entitle the holders to participate in profits, and any special conditions affecting that entitlement;
the date from which the transactions of the transferor company are to be treated for accounting purposes as being those of a transferee company;

any rights or restrictions attaching to shares or other securities in a transferee company to be allotted under the scheme to the holders of shares or other securities in the transferor company to which any special rights or restrictions attach, or the measures proposed concerning them;
any amount of benefit paid or given or intended to be paid or given—

P4para.Text: to any of the experts referred to in section 924 (expert's report), or
to any director of a company involved in the division,

P3para.Text: and the consideration for the payment of benefit.

P2para.Text: The draft terms must also—

P3para.Text: give particulars of the property and liabilities to be transferred (to the extent that these are known to the transferor company) and their allocation among the transferee companies;
make provision for the allocation among and transfer to the transferee companies of any other property and liabilities that the transferor company has acquired or may subsequently acquire; and
specify the allocation to members of the transferor company of shares in the transferee companies and the criteria upon which that allocation is based.

P1group.Title: Publication of draft terms by registrar(division)

P2para.Text: The directors of each company involved in the division must deliver a copy of the draft terms to the registrar.
The registrar must publish in the Gazette notice of receipt by him from that company of a copy of the draft terms.
That notice must be published at least one month before the date of any meeting of that company summoned for the purposes of approving the scheme.
The requirements in this section are subject to section 921A (publication of draft terms on company website) and section 934 (power of court to exclude certain requirements).

Title.Addition: Publication of draft terms on company website (division)

Text.Addition: Section 921 does not apply in respect of a company if the conditions in subsections (2) to (6) are met.
The first condition is that the draft terms are made available on a website which—
is maintained by or on behalf of the company, and
identifies the company.
The second condition is that neither access to the draft terms on the website nor the supply of a hard copy of them from the website is conditional on payment of a fee or otherwise restricted.
The third condition is that the directors of the company deliver to the registrar a notice giving details of the website.
The fourth condition is that the registrar publishes the notice in the Gazette at least one month before the date of any meeting of the company summoned for the purpose of approving the scheme.
The fifth condition is that the draft terms remain available on the website throughout the period beginning one month before, and ending on, the date of any such meeting.

P1group.Title: Approval of members of companies involved in the division

P2para.Text: The scheme must be approved by a majority in number, representing 75% in value, of each class of members of each of the companies involved in the division, present and voting either in person or by proxy at a meeting.
This requirement is subject to sections 931, 931A and 932 (circumstances in which meeting of members not required).

P1group.Title: Directors' explanatory report (division)

P2para.Text: The directors of the transferor and each existing transferee company must draw up and adopt a report.
The report must consist of—

P3para.Text: the required statement explaining the effect of the compromise or arrangement, and
insofar as that statement does not deal with the following matters, a further statement—

P4para.Text: setting out the legal and economic grounds for the draft terms, and in particular for the share exchange ratio and for the criteria on which the allocation to the members of the transferor company of shares in the transferee companies was based, and
specifying any special valuation difficulties.

Text.Addition: In subsection (2) “the required statement explaining the effect of the compromise or arrangement” means—
in a case where a meeting is summoned under section 896 in relation to the compromise or arrangement, the statement required by section 897;
in a case where a meeting is summoned under section 901C in relation to the compromise or arrangement, the statement required by section 901D.

P2para.Text: The report must also state—

P3para.Text: whether a report has been made to any transferee company under section 593 (valuation of non-cash consideration for shares), and
if so, whether that report has been delivered to the registrar of companies.

P2para.Text: The requirement in this section is subject to section 933 (agreement to dispense with reports etc) and section 933A (certain requirements excluded where shareholders given proportional rights).

P1group.Title: Expert's report (division)

P2para.Text: An expert's report must be drawn up on behalf of each company involved in the division.
The report required is a written report on the draft terms to the members of the company.
The court may on the joint application of the companies involved in the division approve the appointment of a joint expert to draw up a single report on behalf of all those companies.
If no such appointment is made, there must be a separate expert's report to the members of each company involved in the division drawn up by a separate expert appointed on behalf of that company.
The expert must be a person who—

P3para.Text: is eligible for appointment as a statutory auditor (see section 1212), and
meets the independence requirement in section 936.

P2para.Text: The expert's report must—

P3para.Text: indicate the method or methods used to arrive at the share exchange ratio;

give an opinion as to whether the method or methods used are reasonable in all the circumstances of the case, indicate the values arrived at using each such method and (if there is more than one method) give an opinion on the relative importance attributed to such methods in arriving at the value decided on;
describe any special valuation difficulties that have arisen;
state whether in the expert's opinion the share exchange ratio is reasonable; and
in the case of a valuation made by a person other than himself (see section 935), state that it appeared to him reasonable to arrange for it to be so made or to accept a valuation so made.

P2para.Text: The expert (or each of them) has—

P3para.Text: the right of access to all such documents of the companies involved in the division, and
the right to require from the companies' officers all such information,

P2para.Text: as he thinks necessary for the purposes of making his report.
The requirement in this section is subject to section 933 (agreement to dispense with reports etc) and section 933A (certain requirements excluded where shareholders given proportional rights).

P1group.Title: Supplementary accounting statement (division)

Text.Substitution: This section applies if the last annual accounts of a company involved in the division relate to a financial year ending before—
the date seven months before the first meeting of the company summoned for the purposes of approving the scheme, or
if no meeting of the company is required (by virtue of section 931
or 932), the date six months before the directors of the company adopt the draft terms of the scheme.

If the company has not made public a half-yearly financial report relating to a period ending on or after the date mentioned in subsection (1), the directors of the company must prepare a supplementary accounting statement.

P2para.Text: That statement must consist of—

P3para.Text: a balance sheet dealing with the state of affairs of the company as at a date not more than three months before the draft terms were adopted by the directors, and

where the company would be required under section 399 to prepare group accounts if that date were the last day of a financial year, a consolidated balance sheet dealing with the state of affairs of the company and the undertakings that would be included in such a consolidation.

P2para.Text: The requirements of this Act ... as to the balance sheet forming part of a company's annual accounts, and the matters to be included in notes to it, apply to the balance sheet required for an accounting statement under this section, with such modifications as are necessary by reason of its being prepared otherwise than as at the last day of a financial year.
The provisions of section 414 as to the approval and signing of accounts apply to the balance sheet required for an accounting statement under this section.

Text.Addition: In this section “
” means a report of that description required to be made public by rules under section 89A of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (transparency rules).

P2para.Text: The requirement in this section is subject to section 933 (agreement to dispense with reports etc) and section 933A (certain requirements excluded where shareholders given proportional rights).

P1group.Title: Inspection of documents (division)

P2para.Text: The members of each company involved in the division must be able, during the period specified below—

P3para.Text: to inspect at the registered office of that company copies of the documents listed below relating to that company and every other company involved in the division, and
to obtain copies of those documents or any part of them on request free of charge.

P2para.Text: The period referred to above is the period—

P3para.Text: beginning one month before, and
ending on the date of,

P2para.Text: the first meeting of the members, or any class of members, of the company for the purposes of approving the scheme.
The documents referred to above are—

P3para.Text: the draft terms;
the directors' explanatory report;
the expert's report;

the company's annual accounts and reports for the last three financial years ending on or before the first meeting of the members, or any class of members, of the company summoned for the purposes of approving the scheme; . . .
any supplementary accounting statement required by section 925; and

Text.Addition: if no statement is required by section 925 because the company has made public a recent half-yearly financial report (see subsection (1A) of that section), that report.
The requirement in subsection (1)(a) is subject to section 926A(1) (publication of documents on company website).

P2para.Text: The requirements in subsection (3)(b), (c) and (e) are subject to section 933 (agreement to dispense with reports etc) , section 933A (certain requirements excluded where shareholders given proportional rights) and section 934 (power of court to exclude certain requirements).

Text.Addition: Section 1145 (right to hard copy) does not apply to a document sent or supplied in accordance with subsection (1)(b) to a member who has consented to information being sent or supplied by the company by electronic means and has not revoked that consent.
Part 4 of Schedule 5 (communications by means of a website) does not apply for the purposes of subsection (1)(b) (but see section 926A(5)).

Title.Addition: Publication of documents on company website (division)

Text.Addition: Section 926(1)(a) does not apply to a document if the conditions in subsections (2) to (4) are met in relation to that document. This is subject to subsection (6).
The first condition is that the document is made available on a website which—
is maintained by or on behalf of the company, and
identifies the company.
The second condition is that access to the document on the website is not conditional on payment of a fee or otherwise restricted.

The third condition is that the document remains available on the website throughout the period beginning one month before, and ending on, the date of any meeting of the company summoned for the purpose of approving the scheme.
A person is able to obtain a copy of a document as required by section 926(1)(b) if—
the conditions in subsections (2) and (3) are met in relation to that document, and
the person is able, throughout the period specified in subsection (4)—
i)to retain a copy of the document as made available on the website, and
to produce a hard copy of it.

Where members of a company are able to obtain copies of a document only as mentioned in subsection (5), section 926(1)(a) applies to that document even if the conditions in subsections (2) to (4) are met.

P1group.Title: Report on material changes of assets of transferor company (division)

P2para.Text: The directors of the transferor company must report—

P3para.Text: to every meeting of the members, or any class of members, of that company summoned for the purpose of agreeing to the scheme, and
to the directors of each existing transferee company,

P2para.Text: any material changes in the property and liabilities of the transferor company between the date when the draft terms were adopted and the date of the meeting in question.
The directors of each existing transferee company must in turn—

P3para.Text: report those matters to every meeting of the members, or any class of members, of that company summoned for the purpose of agreeing to the scheme, or
send a report of those matters to every member entitled to receive notice of such a meeting.

P2para.Text: The requirement in this section is subject to section 933 (agreement to dispense with reports etc) and section 933A (certain requirements excluded where shareholders given proportional rights).

P1group.Title: Approval of articles of new transferee company (division)

P2para.Text: The articles of every new transferee company, or a draft of them, must be approved by ordinary resolution of the transferor company.

Text.Addition: Subsection (1) does not apply in the case of a compromise or arrangement to be sanctioned under Part 26A.

P1group.Title: Protection of holders of securities to which special rights attached (division)

P2para.Text: The scheme must provide that where any securities of the transferor company (other than shares) to which special rights are attached are held by a person otherwise than as a member or creditor of the company, that person is to receive rights in a transferee company of equivalent value.
Subsection (1) does not apply if—

P3para.Text: the holder has agreed otherwise, or
the holder is, or under the scheme is to be, entitled to have the securities purchased by a transferee company on terms that the court considers reasonable.

Title.Substitution: No allotment of shares to transferor company or its nominee (division)

Text.Substitution: The scheme must not provide for any shares in a transferee company to be allotted to—
the transferor company (or its nominee) in respect of shares in the transferor company held by the transferor company itself (or its nominee); or
a transferee company (or its nominee) in respect of shares in the transferor company held by the transferee company (or its nominee).

Title.Emphasis: Exceptions where shares of transferor company held by transferee company

P1group.Title: Circumstances in which meeting of members of transferor company not required (division)

P2para.Text: This section applies in the case of a division where all of the shares or other securities of the transferor company carrying the right to vote at general meetings of the company are held by or on behalf of one or more existing transferee companies.

It is not necessary for the scheme to be approved by a meeting of the members, or any class of members, of the transferor company if the court is satisfied that the following conditions have been complied with.

Text.Substitution: The first condition is that either subsection (3A) or subsection (3B) is satisfied.

This subsection is satisfied if publication of notice of receipt of the draft terms by the registrar took place in respect of all the companies involved in the division at least one month before the date of the court's order.
This subsection is satisfied if—
the conditions in section 921A(2) to (4) are met in respect of each of the companies involved in the division,
in each case, the registrar published the notice mentioned in subsection (4) of that section in the Gazette at least one month before the date of the court's order, and
the draft terms remained available on the website throughout the period beginning one month before, and ending on, that date.
The second condition is that subsection (4A) or (4B) is satisfied for each of the documents listed in the applicable paragraphs of section 926(3) relating to every company involved in the division.

This subsection is satisfied for a document if the members of every company involved in the division were able during the period beginning one month before, and ending on, the date of the court's order to inspect that document at the registered office of their company.
This subsection is satisfied for a document if—
the document is made available on a website which is maintained by or on behalf of the company to which it relates and identifies the company,
access to the document on the website is not conditional on payment of a fee or otherwise restricted, and
the document remains available on the website throughout the period beginning one month before, and ending on, the date of the court's order.

The third condition is that the members of every company involved in the division were able to obtain copies of the documents mentioned in subsection (4), or any part of those documents, on request and free of charge, throughout the period beginning one month before, and ending on, the date of the court's order.
For the purposes of subsection (4C)—
section 926A(5) applies as it applies for the purposes of section 926(1)(b), and
Part 4 of Schedule 5 (communications by means of a website) does not apply.

P2para.Text: The fourth condition is that the directors of the transferor company have sent—

P3para.Text: to every member who would have been entitled to receive notice of a meeting to agree to the scheme (had any such meeting been called), and
to the directors of every existing transferee company,

P2para.Text: a report of any material change in the property and liabilities of the transferor company between the date when the terms were adopted by the directors and the date one month before the date of the court's order.

Title.Addition: Other circumstances in which meeting of members of transferor company not required (division)

Text.Addition: In the case of a compromise or arrangement to be sanctioned under Part 26A, it is not necessary for the scheme to be approved by the members of the transferor company.

P1group.Title: Circumstances in which meeting of members of transferee company not required (division)

P2para.Text: In the case of a division, it is not necessary for the scheme to be approved by the members of a transferee company if the court is satisfied that the following conditions have been complied with in relation to that company.

Text.Substitution: The first condition is that either subsection (2A) or subsection (2B) is satisfied.

This subsection is satisfied if publication of notice of receipt of the draft terms by the registrar took place in respect of the transferee company at least one month before the date of the first meeting of members of the transferor company summoned for the purposes of agreeing to the scheme.
This subsection is satisfied if—
the conditions in section 921A(2) to (4) are met in respect of the transferee company,

the registrar published the notice mentioned in subsection (4) of that section in the Gazette at least one month before the date of the first meeting of members of the transferor company summoned for the purposes of agreeing to the scheme, and
the draft terms remained available on the website throughout the period beginning one month before, and ending on, that date.

The second condition is that subsection (3A) or (3B) is satisfied for each of the documents listed in the applicable paragraphs of section 926(3) relating to the transferee company and every other company involved in the division.

This subsection is satisfied for a document if the members of the transferee company were able during the period beginning one month before, and ending on, the date mentioned in subsection (2A) to inspect that document at the registered office of that company.
This subsection is satisfied for a document if—
the document is made available on a website which is maintained by or on behalf of the transferee company and identifies the company,
access to the document on the website is not conditional on payment of a fee or otherwise restricted, and
the document remains available on the website throughout the period beginning one month before, and ending on, the date mentioned in subsection (2A).

The third condition is that the members of the transferee company were able to obtain copies of the documents mentioned in subsection (3), or any part of those documents, on request and free of charge, throughout the period beginning one month before, and ending on, the date mentioned in subsection (2A).
For the purposes of subsection (3C)—
section 926A(5) applies as it applies for the purposes of section 926(1)(b), and
Part 4 of Schedule 5 (communications by means of a website) does not apply.

P2para.Text: The fourth condition is that—

P3para.Text: one or more members of that company, who together held not less than 5% of the paid-up capital of the company which carried the right to vote at general meetings of the company (excluding any shares in the company held as treasury shares) would have been able, during that period, to require a meeting of each class of members to be called for the purpose of deciding whether or not to agree to the scheme, and
no such requirement was made.

P2para.Text: The first, second and third conditions above are subject to section 934 (power of court to exclude certain requirements).

P1group.Title: Agreement to dispense with reports etc (division)

P2para.Text: If all members holding shares in, and all persons holding other securities of, the companies involved in the division, being shares or securities that carry a right to vote in general meetings of the company in question, so agree, the following requirements do not apply.
The requirements that may be dispensed with under this section are—

P3para.Text: the requirements of—

P4para.Text: section 923 (directors' explanatory report),
section 924 (expert's report),
section 925 (supplementary accounting statement), and
section 927 (report on material changes in assets of transferor company); and

P3para.Text: the requirements of section 926 (inspection of documents) so far as relating to any document required to be drawn up under the provisions mentioned in paragraph (a)(i), (ii) or (iii) above.

P2para.Text: For the purposes of this section—

P3para.Text: the members, or holders of other securities, of a company, and
whether shares or other securities carry a right to vote in general meetings of the company,

P2para.Text: are determined as at the date of the relevant application.

Text.Addition: In subsection (3) “the relevant application” means—
in the case of a compromise or arrangement to be sanctioned under Part 26, the application to the court under section 896;
in the case of a compromise or arrangement to be sanctioned under Part 26A, the application to the court under section 901C(1).

Title.Addition: Certain requirements excluded where shareholders given proportional rights (division)

Text.Addition: This section applies in the case of a division where each of the transferee companies is a new company.

If all the shares in each of the transferee companies are to be allotted to the members of the transferor company in proportion to their rights in the allotted share capital of the transferor company, the following requirements do not apply.
The requirements which do not apply are—
the requirements of—
i)section 923 (directors' explanatory report),
section 924 (expert's report),
section 925 (supplementary accounting statement), and
section 927 (report on material changes in assets of transferor company); and
the requirements of section 926 (inspection of documents) so far as relating to any document required to be drawn up under the provisions mentioned in paragraph (a)(i), (ii) or (iii) above.

P1group.Title: Power of court to exclude certain requirements (division)

P2para.Text: In the case of a division, the court may by order direct that—

P3para.Text: in relation to any company involved in the division, the requirements of—

P4para.Text: section 921 (publication of draft terms), and
section 926 (inspection of documents),

P3para.Text: do not apply, and

in relation to an existing transferee company, section 932 (circumstances in which meeting of members of transferee company not required) has effect with the omission of the first, second and third conditions specified in that section,

P2para.Text: if the court is satisfied that the following conditions will be fulfilled in relation to that company.
The first condition is that the members of that company will have received, or will have been able to obtain free of charge, copies of the documents listed in section 926—

P3para.Text: in time to examine them before the date of the first meeting of the members, or any class of members, of that company summoned for the purposes of agreeing to the scheme, or
in the case of an existing transferee company where in the circumstances described in section 932 no meeting is held, in time to require a meeting as mentioned in subsection (4) of that section.

P2para.Text: The second condition is that the creditors of that company will have received or will have been able to obtain free of charge copies of the draft terms in time to examine them—

P3para.Text: before the date of the first meeting of the members, or any class of members, of the company summoned for the purposes of agreeing to the scheme, or
in the circumstances mentioned in subsection (2)(b) above, at the same time as the members of the company.

P2para.Text: The third condition is that no prejudice would be caused to the members or creditors of the transferor company or any transferee company by making the order in question.

P1group.Title: Expert's report: valuation by another person

P2para.Text: Where it appears to an expert—

P3para.Text: that a valuation is reasonably necessary to enable him to draw up his report, and
that it is reasonable for that valuation, or part of it, to be made by (or for him to accept a valuation made by) another person who—

P4para.Text: appears to him to have the requisite knowledge and experience to make the valuation or that part of it, and
meets the independence requirement in section 936,

P2para.Text: he may arrange for or accept such a valuation, together with a report which will enable him to make his own report under section 909 or 924.
Where any valuation is made by a person other than the expert himself, the latter's report must state that fact and must also—

P3para.Text: state the former's name and what knowledge and experience he has to carry out the valuation, and
describe so much of the undertaking, property and liabilities as was valued by the other person, and the method used to value them, and specify the date of the valuation.

P1group.Title: Experts and valuers: independence requirement

P2para.Text: A person meets the independence requirement for the purposes of section 909 or 924 (expert's report) or section 935 (valuation by another person) only if—

P3para.Text: he is not—

P4para.Text: an officer or employee of any of the companies concerned in the scheme, or
a partner or employee of such a person, or a partnership of which such a person is a partner;

P3para.Text: he is not—

P4para.Text: an officer or employee of an associated undertaking of any of the companies concerned in the scheme, or
a partner or employee of such a person, or a partnership of which such a person is a partner; and

P3para.Text: there does not exist between—

P4para.Text: the person or an associate of his, and
any of the companies concerned in the scheme or an associated undertaking of such a company,

P3para.Text: a connection of any such description as may be specified by regulations made by the Secretary of State.

P2para.Text: An auditor of a company is not regarded as an officer or employee of the company for this purpose.
For the purposes of this section—

P3para.Text: the “companies concerned in the scheme” means every transferor and existing transferee company;
“associated undertaking”, in relation to a company, means—

P4para.Text: a parent undertaking or subsidiary undertaking of the company, or
a subsidiary undertaking of a parent undertaking of the company; and

P3para.Text: “associate” has the meaning given by section 937.

P2para.Text: Regulations under this section are subject to negative resolution procedure.

P1group.Title: Experts and valuers: meaning of “associate”

P2para.Text: This section defines “associate” for the purposes of section 936 (experts and valuers: independence requirement).
In relation to an individual, “associate” means—

P3para.Text: that individual's spouse or civil partner or minor child or step-child,
any body corporate of which that individual is a director, and
any employee or partner of that individual.

P2para.Text: In relation to a body corporate, “associate” means—

P3para.Text: any body corporate of which that body is a director,
any body corporate in the same group as that body, and
any employee or partner of that body or of any body corporate in the same group.

P2para.Text: In relation to a partnership that is a legal person under the law by which it is governed, “associate” means—

P3para.Text: any body corporate of which that partnership is a director,
any employee of or partner in that partnership, and
any person who is an associate of a partner in that partnership.

P2para.Text: In relation to a partnership that is not a legal person under the law by which it is governed, “associate” means any person who is an associate of any of the partners.
In this section, in relation to a limited liability partnership, for “director” read “member”.

P1group.Title: Power of court to summon meeting of members or creditors of existing transferee company

P2para.Text: The court may order a meeting of—

P3para.Text: the members of an existing transferee company, or any class of them, or
the creditors of an existing transferee company, or any class of them,

P2para.Text: to be summoned in such manner as the court directs.
An application for such an order may be made by—

P3para.Text: the company concerned,
a member or creditor of the company, or

Text.Substitution: if the company is being wound up, the liquidator, or
if the company is in administration, the administrator.

Text.Addition: Section 323 (representation of corporations at meetings) applies to a meeting of creditors under this section as to a meeting of the company (references to a member being read as references to a creditor).

P1group.Title: Court to fix date for transfer of undertaking etc of transferor company

P2para.Text: Where the court sanctions the compromise or arrangement, it must—

P3para.Text: in the order sanctioning the compromise or arrangement, or
in a subsequent order under section 900 or, as the case may be, section 901J (powers of court to facilitate reconstruction or amalgamation),

P2para.Text: fix a date on which the transfer (or transfers) to the transferee company (or transferee companies) of the undertaking, property and liabilities of the transferor company is (or are) to take place.
Any such order that provides for the dissolution of the transferor company must fix the same date for the dissolution.

If it is necessary for the transferor company to take steps to ensure that the undertaking, property and liabilities are fully transferred, the court must fix a date, not later than six months after the date fixed under subsection (1), by which such steps must be taken.
In that case, the court may postpone the dissolution of the transferor company until that date.

The court may postpone or further postpone the date fixed under subsection (3) if it is satisfied that the steps mentioned cannot be completed by the date (or latest date) fixed under that subsection.

P1group.Title: Liability of transferee companies for each other's defaults

P2para.Text: In the case of a division, each transferee company is jointly and severally liable for any liability transferred to any other transferee company under the scheme to the extent that the other company has made default in satisfying that liability.
This is subject to the following provisions.

If, in the case of a compromise or arrangement to be sanctioned under Part 26, a majority in number representing 75% in value of the creditors or any class of creditors of the transferor company, present and voting either in person or by proxy at a meeting summoned for the purposes of agreeing to the scheme, so agree, subsection (1) does not apply in relation to the liabilities owed to the creditors or that class of creditors.

Text.Addition: If, in the case of a compromise or arrangement to be sanctioned under Part 26A, a number representing 75% in value of the creditors or any class of creditors of the transferor company, present and voting either in person or by proxy at a meeting summoned for the purposes of agreeing to the scheme, so agree, subsection (1) does not apply in relation to the liabilities owed to the creditors or that class of creditors.

P2para.Text: A transferee company is not liable under this section for an amount greater than the net value transferred to it under the scheme.
The “net value transferred” is the value at the time of the transfer of the property transferred to it under the scheme less the amount at that date of the liabilities so transferred.

Title.Addition: Disregard of website failures beyond control of company

Text.Addition: A failure to make information or a document available on the website throughout a period specified in any of the provisions mentioned in subsection (2) is to be disregarded if—
it is made available on the website for part of that period, and
the failure to make it available throughout that period is wholly attributable to circumstances that it would not be reasonable to have expected the company to prevent or avoid.
The provisions referred to above are—
section 906A(6),
section 911A(4),
section 916(3B) and (4B),
section 917(3B) and (4B),
section 918(2B) and (3B),
section 921A(6),
section 926A(4),
section 931(3B) and (4B), and
section 932(2B) and (3B).

P1group.Title: Meaning of “liabilities” and “property”

P1para.Text: In this Part—

Para.Text: “liabilities” includes duties;
“property” includes property, rights and powers of every description.

P1group.Title: The Panel

P2para.Text: The body known as the Panel on Takeovers and Mergers (“the Panel”) is to have the functions conferred on it by or under this Chapter.
The Panel may do anything that it considers necessary or expedient for the purposes of, or in connection with, its functions.
The Panel may make arrangements for any of its functions to be discharged by—

P3para.Text: a committee or sub-committee of the Panel, or
an officer or member of staff of the Panel, or a person acting as such.

P2para.Text: This is subject to section 943(4) and (5).

P1group.Title: Rules

Text.Substitution: The Panel must make rules—
giving effect to the general principles in Part 1 of Schedule 1C, and
in accordance with Part 2 of that Schedule.

Text.Addition: Rules must specify the percentage of voting rights that gives a person control of a company for the purposes of this Chapter and how it is to be calculated.

P2para.Text: Rules made by the Panel may also make other provision—

P3para.Text: for or in connection with the regulation of—

P4para.Text: takeover bids,
merger transactions, and
transactions (not falling within sub-paragraph (i) or (ii)) that have or may have, directly or indirectly, an effect on the ownership or control of companies;

P3para.Text: for or in connection with the regulation of things done in consequence of, or otherwise in relation to, any such bid or transaction;
about cases where—

P4para.Text: any such bid or transaction is, or has been, contemplated or apprehended, or
an announcement is made denying that any such bid or transaction is intended.

P2para.Text: The provision that may be made under subsection (2) includes, in particular, provision for a matter that is, or is similar to, a matter provided for by the Panel in the City Code on Takeovers and Mergers as it had effect immediately before the passing of this Act.
In relation to rules made by virtue of section 957 (fees and charges), functions under this section may be discharged either by the Panel itself or by a committee of the Panel (but not otherwise).
In relation to rules of any other description, the Panel must discharge its functions under this section by a committee of the Panel.
Section 1 (meaning of “company”) does not apply for the purposes of this section.
In this section “takeover bid” includes a takeover bid within the meaning given by paragraph 20(1) of Schedule 1C.
A reference to rules in the following provisions of this Chapter is to rules under this section.

P1group.Title: Further provisions about rules

P2para.Text: Rules may—

P3para.Text: make different provision for different purposes;
make provision subject to exceptions or exemptions;
contain incidental, supplemental, consequential or transitional provision;
authorise the Panel to dispense with or modify the application of rules in particular cases and by reference to any circumstances.

P2para.Text: Rules made by virtue of paragraph (d) must require the Panel to give reasons for acting as mentioned in that paragraph.
Rules must be made by an instrument in writing.
Immediately after an instrument containing rules is made, the text must be made available to the public, with or without payment, in whatever way the Panel thinks appropriate.
A person is not to be taken to have contravened a rule if he shows that at the time of the alleged contravention the text of the rule had not been made available as required by subsection (3).

The production of a printed copy of an instrument purporting to be made by the Panel on which is endorsed a certificate signed by an officer of the Panel authorised by it for that purpose and stating—

P3para.Text: that the instrument was made by the Panel,
that the copy is a true copy of the instrument, and
that on a specified date the text of the instrument was made available to the public as required by subsection (3),

P2para.Text: is evidence (or in Scotland sufficient evidence) of the facts stated in the certificate.
A certificate purporting to be signed as mentioned in subsection (5) is to be treated as having been properly signed unless the contrary is shown.

A person who wishes in any legal proceedings to rely on an instrument by which rules are made may require the Panel to endorse a copy of the instrument with a certificate of the kind mentioned in subsection (5).

P1group.Title: Rulings

P2para.Text: The Panel may give rulings on the interpretation, application or effect of rules.
To the extent and in the circumstances specified in rules, and subject to any review or appeal, a ruling has binding effect.

P1group.Title: Directions

P1para.Text: Rules may contain provision conferring power on the Panel to give any direction that appears to the Panel to be necessary in order—

P3para.Text: to restrain a person from acting (or continuing to act) in breach of rules;
to restrain a person from doing (or continuing to do) a particular thing, pending determination of whether that or any other conduct of his is or would be a breach of rules;
otherwise to secure compliance with rules.

P1group.Title: Power to require documents and information

P2para.Text: The Panel may by notice in writing require a person—

P3para.Text: to produce any documents that are specified or described in the notice;
to provide, in the form and manner specified in the notice, such information as may be specified or described in the notice.

P2para.Text: A requirement under subsection (1) must be complied with—

P3para.Text: at a place specified in the notice, and
before the end of such reasonable period as may be so specified.

P2para.Text: This section applies only to documents and information reasonably required in connection with the exercise by the Panel of its functions.
The Panel may require—

P3para.Text: any document produced to be authenticated, or
any information provided (whether in a document or otherwise) to be verified,

P2para.Text: in such manner as it may reasonably require.
The Panel may authorise a person to exercise any of its powers under this section.
A person exercising a power by virtue of subsection (5) must, if required to do so, produce evidence of his authority to exercise the power.
The production of a document in pursuance of this section does not affect any lien that a person has on the document.
The Panel may take copies of or extracts from a document produced in pursuance of this section.
A reference in this section to the production of a document includes a reference to the production of—

P3para.Text: a hard copy of information recorded otherwise than in hard copy form, or
information in a form from which a hard copy can be readily obtained.

P2para.Text: A person is not required by this section to disclose documents or information in respect of which a claim to legal professional privilege (in Scotland, to confidentiality of communications) could be maintained in legal proceedings.

P1group.Title: Restrictions on disclosure

P2para.Text: This section applies to information (in whatever form)—

P3para.Text: relating to the private affairs of an individual, or
relating to any particular business,

P2para.Text: that is provided to the Panel in connection with the exercise of its functions.

No such information may, during the lifetime of the individual or so long as the business continues to be carried on, be disclosed without the consent of that individual or (as the case may be) the person for the time being carrying on that business.
Subsection (2) does not apply to any disclosure of information that—

P3para.Text: is made for the purpose of facilitating the carrying out by the Panel of any of its functions,
is made to a person specified in Part 1 of Schedule 2,
is of a description specified in Part 2 of that Schedule, or
is made in accordance with Part 3 of that Schedule.

P2para.Text: The Secretary of State may amend Schedule 2 by order subject to negative resolution procedure.
An order under subsection (4) must not—

P3para.Text: amend Part 1 of Schedule 2 by specifying a person unless the person exercises functions of a public nature (whether or not he exercises any other function);

amend Part 2 of Schedule 2 by adding or modifying a description of disclosure unless the purpose for which the disclosure is permitted is likely to facilitate the exercise of a function of a public nature;

amend Part 3 of Schedule 2 so as to have the effect of permitting disclosures to be made to a body other than one that exercises functions of a public nature in a country or territory outside the United Kingdom.

P2para.Text: Subsection (2) does not apply to—

P3para.Text: the disclosure by an authority within subsection (7) of information disclosed to it by the Panel in reliance on subsection (3);
the disclosure of such information by anyone who has obtained it directly or indirectly from an authority within subsection (7).

P2para.Text: The authorities within this subsection are—

Text.Substitution: the Financial Conduct Authority;
the Prudential Regulation Authority;
the Bank of England;

P2para.Text: This section does not prohibit the disclosure of information if the information is or has been available to the public from any other source.
Nothing in this section authorises the making of a disclosure in contravention of the data protection legislation.

P1group.Title: Offence of disclosure in contravention of section 948

P2para.Text: A person who discloses information in contravention of section 948 is guilty of an offence, unless—

P3para.Text: he did not know, and had no reason to suspect, that the information had been provided as mentioned in section 948(1), or
he took all reasonable steps and exercised all due diligence to avoid the commission of the offence.

P2para.Text: A person guilty of an offence under this section is liable—

P3para.Text: on conviction on indictment, to imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years or a fine (or both);
on summary conviction—

P4para.Text: in England and Wales, to imprisonment for a term not exceeding twelve months or to a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum (or both);
in Scotland or Northern Ireland, to imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months, or to a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum (or both).

P2para.Text: Where a company or other body corporate commits an offence under this section, an offence is also committed by every officer of the company or other body corporate who is in default.

P1group.Title: Panel's duty of co-operation

P2para.Text: The Panel must take such steps as it considers appropriate to co-operate with—

Text.Substitution: the Financial Conduct Authority;
the Prudential Regulation Authority;
the Bank of England;

P3para.Text: any other person or body that exercises functions of a public nature, under legislation in any country or territory outside the United Kingdom, that appear to the Panel to be similar to its own functions or those of the Financial Conduct Authority or the Prudential Regulation Authority or similar to the regulatory functions of the Bank of England.

P2para.Text: Co-operation may include the sharing of information that the Panel is not prevented from disclosing.

P1group.Title: Hearings and appeals

P2para.Text: Rules must provide for a decision of the Panel to be subject to review by a committee of the Panel (the “Hearings Committee”) at the instance of such persons affected by the decision as are specified in the rules.
Rules may also confer other functions on the Hearings Committee.

Rules must provide for there to be a right of appeal against a decision of the Hearings Committee to an independent tribunal (the “Takeover Appeal Board”) in such circumstances and subject to such conditions as are specified in the rules.
Rules may contain—

P3para.Text: provision as to matters of procedure in relation to proceedings before the Hearings Committee (including provision imposing time limits);
provision about evidence in such proceedings;
provision as to the powers of the Hearings Committee dealing with a matter referred to it;
provision about enforcement of decisions of the Hearings Committee and the Takeover Appeal Board.

P2para.Text: Rules must contain provision—

P3para.Text: requiring the Panel, when acting in relation to any proceedings before the Hearings Committee or the Takeover Appeal Board, to do so by an officer or member of staff of the Panel (or a person acting as such);
preventing a person who is or has been a member of the committee mentioned in section 943(5) from being a member of the Hearings Committee or the Takeover Appeal Board;
preventing a person who is a member of the committee mentioned in section 943(5), of the Hearings Committee or of the Takeover Appeal Board from acting as mentioned in paragraph (a).

P1group.Title: Sanctions

P2para.Text: Rules may contain provision conferring power on the Panel to impose sanctions on a person who has—

P3para.Text: acted in breach of rules, or
failed to comply with a direction given by virtue of section 946.

P2para.Text: Subsection (3) applies where rules made by virtue of subsection (1) confer power on the Panel to impose a sanction of a kind not provided for by the City Code on Takeovers and Mergers as it had effect immediately before the passing of this Act.
The Panel must prepare a statement (a “policy statement”) of its policy with respect to—

P3para.Text: the imposition of the sanction in question, and
where the sanction is in the nature of a financial penalty, the amount of the penalty that may be imposed.

P2para.Text: An element of the policy must be that, in making a decision about any such matter, the Panel has regard to the factors mentioned in subsection (4).
The factors are—

P3para.Text: the seriousness of the breach or failure in question in relation to the nature of the rule or direction contravened;
the extent to which the breach or failure was deliberate or reckless;
whether the person on whom the sanction is to be imposed is an individual.

P2para.Text: The Panel may at any time revise a policy statement.
The Panel must prepare a draft of any proposed policy statement (or revised policy statement) and consult such persons about the draft as the Panel considers appropriate.
The Panel must publish, in whatever way it considers appropriate, any policy statement (or revised policy statement) that it prepares.

In exercising, or deciding whether to exercise, its power to impose a sanction within subsection (2) in the case of any particular breach or failure, the Panel must have regard to any relevant policy statement published and in force at the time when the breach or failure occurred.

P1group.Title: Failure to comply with rules about bid documentation

P2para.Text: This section applies where a takeover bid is made for a company that has securities carrying voting rights admitted to trading on a regulated market in the United Kingdom.
Where an offer document published in respect of the bid does not comply with offer document rules, an offence is committed by—

P3para.Text: the person making the bid, and
where the person making the bid is a body of persons, any director, officer or member of that body who caused the document to be published.

P2para.Text: A person commits an offence under subsection (2) only if—

P3para.Text: he knew that the offer document did not comply, or was reckless as to whether it complied, and
he failed to take all reasonable steps to secure that it did comply.

P2para.Text: Where a response document published in respect of the bid does not comply with response document rules, an offence is committed by any director or other officer of the company referred to in subsection (1) who—

P3para.Text: knew that the response document did not comply, or was reckless as to whether it complied, and
failed to take all reasonable steps to secure that it did comply.

P2para.Text: Where an offence is committed under subsection (2)(b) or (4) by a company or other body corporate (“the relevant body”)—

P3para.Text: subsection (2)(b) has effect as if the reference to a director, officer or member of the person making the bid included a reference to a director, officer or member of the relevant body;
subsection (4) has effect as if the reference to a director or other officer of the company referred to in subsection (1) included a reference to a director, officer or member of the relevant body.

P2para.Text: A person guilty of an offence under this section is liable—

P3para.Text: on conviction on indictment, to a fine;
on summary conviction, to a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.

P2para.Text: Nothing in this section affects any power of the Panel in relation to the enforcement of its rules.
Section 1 (meaning of “company”) does not apply for the purposes of this section.
In this section—

Para.Text: “designated” means designated in rules;
“offer document” means a document required to be published by rules made in accordance with paragraph 12(1) to (3) of Schedule 1C;

Text.Substitution: “offer document rules” means rules under section 943(1) designated as rules made in accordance with paragraph 12(4) of Schedule 1C;

Para.Text: “response document” means a document required to be published by rules made in accordance with paragraph 18 of Schedule 1C;

Text.Substitution: “response document rules” means rules under section 943(1) designated as rules made in accordance with paragraph 18(1) of Schedule 1C;

Para.Text: “securities” means shares or debentures;
“takeover bid” has the meaning given by paragraph 20(1) of Schedule 1C;
“voting rights” means rights to vote at general meetings of the company in question, including rights that arise only in certain circumstances.

P1group.Title: Compensation

P2para.Text: Rules may confer power on the Panel to order a person to pay such compensation as it thinks just and reasonable if he is in breach of a rule the effect of which is to require the payment of money.
Rules made by virtue of this section may include provision for the payment of interest (including compound interest).

P1group.Title: Enforcement by the court

P2para.Text: If, on the application of the Panel, the court is satisfied—

P3para.Text: that there is a reasonable likelihood that a person will contravene a rule-based requirement, or
that a person has contravened a rule-based requirement or a disclosure requirement,

P2para.Text: the court may make any order it thinks fit to secure compliance with the requirement.
In subsection (1) “the court” means the High Court or, in Scotland, the Court of Session.
Except as provided by subsection (1), no person—

P3para.Text: has a right to seek an injunction, or
in Scotland, has title or interest to seek an interdict or an order for specific performance,

P2para.Text: to prevent a person from contravening (or continuing to contravene) a rule-based requirement or a disclosure requirement.
In this section—

Para.Text: “contravene” includes fail to comply;
“disclosure requirement” means a requirement imposed under section 947;
“rule-based requirement” means a requirement imposed by or under rules.

P1group.Title: No action for breach of statutory duty etc

P2para.Text: Contravention of a rule-based requirement or a disclosure requirement does not give rise to any right of action for breach of statutory duty.
Contravention of a rule-based requirement does not make any transaction void or unenforceable or (subject to any provision made by rules) affect the validity of any other thing.
In this section—

P3para.Text: “contravention” includes failure to comply;
“disclosure requirement” and “rule-based requirement” have the same meaning as in section 955.

P1group.Title: Fees and charges

P2para.Text: Rules may provide for fees or charges to be payable to the Panel for the purpose of meeting any part of its expenses.

A reference in this section or section 958 to expenses of the Panel is to any expenses that have been or are to be incurred by the Panel in, or in connection with, the discharge of its functions, including in particular—

P3para.Text: payments in respect of the expenses of the Takeover Appeal Board;
the cost of repaying the principal of, and of paying any interest on, any money borrowed by the Panel;
the cost of maintaining adequate reserves.

P1group.Title: Levy

P2para.Text: For the purpose of meeting any part of the expenses of the Panel, the Secretary of State may by regulations provide for a levy to be payable to the Panel—

P3para.Text: by specified persons or bodies, or persons or bodies of a specified description, or
on transactions, of a specified description, in securities on specified markets.

P2para.Text: In this subsection “specified” means specified in the regulations.
The power to specify (or to specify descriptions of) persons or bodies must be exercised in such a way that the levy is payable only by persons or bodies that appear to the Secretary of State—

P3para.Text: to be capable of being directly affected by the exercise of any of the functions of the Panel, or
otherwise to have a substantial interest in the exercise of any of those functions.

P2para.Text: Regulations under this section may in particular—

P3para.Text: specify the rate of the levy and the period in respect of which it is payable at that rate;
make provision as to the times when, and the manner in which, payments are to be made in respect of the levy.

P2para.Text: In determining the rate of the levy payable in respect of a particular period, the Secretary of State—

P3para.Text: must take into account any other income received or expected by the Panel in respect of that period;
may take into account estimated as well as actual expenses of the Panel in respect of that period.

P2para.Text: The Panel must—

P3para.Text: keep proper accounts in respect of any amounts of levy received by virtue of this section;
prepare, in relation to each period in respect of which any such amounts are received, a statement of account relating to those amounts in such form and manner as is specified in the regulations.

P2para.Text: Those accounts must be audited, and the statement certified, by persons appointed by the Secretary of State.
Regulations under this section—

P3para.Text: are subject to affirmative resolution procedure if subsection (7) applies to them;
otherwise, are subject to negative resolution procedure.

P2para.Text: This subsection applies to—

P3para.Text: the first regulations under this section;
any other regulations under this section that would result in a change in the persons or bodies by whom, or the transactions on which, the levy is payable.

P2para.Text: If a draft of an instrument containing regulations under this section would, apart from this subsection, be treated for the purposes of the Standing Orders of either House of Parliament as a hybrid instrument, it is to proceed in that House as if it were not such an instrument.

P1group.Title: Recovery of fees, charges or levy

P1para.Text: An amount payable by any person or body by virtue of section 957 or 958 is a debt due from that person or body to the Panel, and is recoverable accordingly.

P1group.Title: Panel as party to proceedings

P1para.Text: The Panel is capable (despite being an unincorporated body) of—

P3para.Text: bringing proceedings under this Chapter in its own name;
bringing or defending any other proceedings in its own name.

P1group.Title: Exemption from liability in damages

P2para.Text: Neither the Panel, nor any person within subsection (2), is to be liable in damages for anything done (or omitted to be done) in, or in connection with, the discharge or purported discharge of the Panel's functions.
A person is within this subsection if—

P3para.Text: he is (or is acting as) a member, officer or member of staff of the Panel, or
he is a person authorised under section 947(5).

P2para.Text: Subsection (1) does not apply—

P3para.Text: if the act or omission is shown to have been in bad faith, or

so as to prevent an award of damages in respect of the act or omission on the ground that it was unlawful as a result of section 6(1) of the Human Rights Act 1998 (c. 42) (acts of public authorities incompatible with Convention rights).

P1group.Title: Privilege against self-incrimination

P2para.Text: A statement made by a person in response to—

P3para.Text: a requirement under section 947(1), or
an order made by the court under section 955 to secure compliance with such a requirement,

P2para.Text: may not be used against him in criminal proceedings in which he is charged with an offence to which this subsection applies.
Subsection (1) applies to any offence other than an offence under one of the following provisions (which concern false statements made otherwise than on oath)—

P3para.Text: section 5 of the Perjury Act 1911 (c. 6);
section 44(2) of the Criminal Law (Consolidation) (Scotland) Act 1995 (c. 39);
Article 10 of the Perjury (Northern Ireland) Order 1979 (S.I. 1979/1714 (N.I. 19)).

P1group.Title: Annual reports

P2para.Text: After the end of each financial year the Panel must publish a report.
The report must—

P3para.Text: set out how the Panel's functions were discharged in the year in question;
include the Panel's accounts for that year;
mention any matters the Panel considers to be of relevance to the discharge of its functions.

P1group.Title: Amendments to Financial Services and Markets Act 2000

P2para.Text: The Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (c. 8) is amended as follows.
Section 143 (power to make rules endorsing the City Code on Takeovers and Mergers etc) is repealed.
In section 349 (exceptions from restrictions on disclosure of confidential information), after subsection (3) insert—
Section 348 does not apply to—

P3para.Text: the disclosure by a recipient to which subsection (3B) applies of confidential information disclosed to it by the Authority in reliance on subsection (1);
the disclosure of such information by a person obtaining it directly or indirectly from a recipient to which subsection (3B) applies.

P2para.Text: This subsection applies to—

P3para.Text: the Panel on Takeovers and Mergers;
an authority designated as a supervisory authority for the purposes of Article 4.1 of the Takeovers Directive;

any other person or body that exercises public functions, under legislation in an EEA State other than the United Kingdom, that are similar to the Authority's functions or those of the Panel on Takeovers and Mergers.

P2para.Text: In section 417(1) (definitions), insert at the appropriate place—

P3para.Text: “Takeovers Directive” means Directive 2004/25/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council;

P1group.Title: Power to extend to Isle of Man and Channel Islands

P1para.Text: Her Majesty may by Order in Council direct that any of the provisions of this Chapter extend, with such modifications as may be specified in the Order, to the Isle of Man or any of the Channel Islands.

P1group.Title: Opting in and opting out

P2para.Text: A company may by special resolution (an “opting-in resolution”) opt in for the purposes of this Chapter if the following five conditions are met in relation to the company.
The first condition is that the company has voting shares admitted to trading on a UK regulated market.

Text.Substitution: The second condition is that the company’s articles of association do not contain any restrictions on the transfer of shares or, if they do contain any such restrictions, provide that they are not to apply to—
transfers to the offeror, or at the offeror’s direction to another person, during the offer period, or
transfers to any person at a time during the offer period when the offeror holds shares amounting to not less than 75% in value of all the voting shares in the company.
The third condition is that the company’s articles of association—
do not contain any restrictions on rights to vote at a general meeting of the company, or
if they do contain any such restrictions, provide that they are not to have effect on rights to vote at a general meeting of the company that—
decides whether to take any action which might result in the frustration of the takeover bid, or
is held at a time when the offeror holds shares amounting to not less than 75% in value of all the voting shares in the company,
unless the restrictions are compensated for by specific pecuniary advantages.
The fourth condition is that the company’s articles of association do not contain any other provision which would be incompatible with the requirements of subsection (3C).
Those requirements are—
multiple-vote shares are to carry only one vote each at a general meeting of the company that decides whether to take any action which might result in the frustration of the takeover bid,
multiple-vote shares are to carry only one vote each at a general meeting of the company which—
is the first such meeting to be held after the end of the offer period,
is held at a time when the offeror holds shares amounting to not less than 75% in value of all the voting shares in the company, and
is called at the offeror’s request under section 969 in order to amend the company’s articles of association or to appoint or remove members of the board of directors, and

at a time during the offer period when the offeror holds shares amounting to not less than 75% in value of all the voting shares in the company, shareholders are not to have any extraordinary rights to appoint or remove members of the board of directors.

The references in subsections (3A)(b) and (3C)(a) to voting at a general meeting of the company that decides whether to take any action which might result in the frustration of the takeover bid includes a reference to voting on a written resolution concerned with that question.

For the purposes of subsections (3A)(b)(i) and (3C)(a), action which might result in the frustration of the takeover bid is any action of that kind specified in rules under section 943(1) made in accordance with paragraphs 17 or 18 of Schedule 1C.
The references in subsections (3), (3A) and (3C) to voting shares in the company do not include—
debentures, or
